English: Murang’a government distributes lime to boost coffee production and farmers’ earnings. Coffee farmers in Murang’a County are set to benefit from increased production following the distribution of 9,917 bags of agricultural lime by the county government in an initiative aimed at restoring soil fertility and reviving the coffee sector. The programme, spearheaded by Governor Irungu Kang’ata through the Department of Agriculture, Livestock and Cooperatives, seeks to address soil acidity, improve nutrient uptake and enhance coffee yields, ultimately increasing farmers’ incomes. Each of the distributed bags weighs 50 kilograms, with the total quantity expected to treat approximately 1.98 million coffee trees using the recommended application rate of 250 grams per tree. According to the county administration, improved soil conditions resulting from the lime application are projected to increase coffee production by about four million kilograms during the 2026/2027 harvest season. Based on the average prices paid to farmers last season, the additional production is expected to generate close to Sh. 500 million in extra earnings for coffee growers across the county. Governor Kang’ata said the Coffee Lime Programme forms part of his administration’s broader strategy to revitalize the coffee industry by improving farm productivity and ensuring farmers earn better returns. “We have distributed 9,917 bags of agricultural lime for application to 1,983,400 coffee trees. We expect this intervention to produce an additional 3,966,800 kilograms of coffee during the 2026/2027 season, translating into increased income for our farmers,” said the governor when he met officials from various coffee cooperative societies. He noted that many coffee farms in Murang’a have acidic soils, which reduce the effectiveness of fertilizers and limit crop productivity. The application of agricultural lime helps correct soil acidity, allowing coffee plants to absorb nutrients more efficiently and grow healthier. County Executive Committee Member for Agriculture, Livestock and Cooperatives Kimani Mugo urged farmers to apply the lime correctly to realize the full benefits of the programme. He advised farmers to use the recommended rate of 250 grams per coffee tree saying proper application would improve soil fertility, enhance fertilizer efficiency and promote stronger, more productive coffee bushes. Mugo added that the county government will continue providing extension services to guide farmers on proper soil management and other good agricultural practices aimed at improving coffee quality and yields. He said the initiative is expected to deliver long-term benefits by restoring soil health, reducing soil acidity and creating favourable conditions for sustainable coffee production. Mugo noted that healthier soils will not only increase yields but also improve the quality of coffee enabling farmers to earn better returns in the competitive global coffee market. The lime distribution programme complements other county interventions in the coffee sector, including the provision of subsidized farm inputs, farmer training and support for coffee cooperative societies, all aimed at restoring Murang’a’s position as one of Kenya’s leading coffee-producing counties. By Bernard Munyao and Yvonne Wanja

Athletes and coaches back stronger anti-doping law. Athletes and coaches in Kericho want stiffer penalties imposed for doping offenses, arguing that the current sanctions were short of expectations to deter offenders. The proposals were made during a public participation forum organized by the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya (ADAK) to collect views on the proposed review of the Anti-Doping Act of 2016. The participants aired several concerns that they proposed to be factored in the amendment of the Anti-Doping Act of 2016. Speaking during a public participation forum held at the Kericho Teachers Training College, World Athletics U20 Championships gold medalist Vincent Keter urged Parliament to strengthen the Anti-Doping Act by imposing stiffer penalties on athletes and athlete support personnel found guilty by doping, saying tougher sanctions would help deter repeat offenders. The middle distance runner who specializes in the 1500m and 800m track disciplines said some athletes are willing to take the risk of doping because they can win prize money pay the prescribed fines if caught and later return to competition, undermining efforts to protect the integrity of the sport. “The penalties should be tougher. Some athletes take shortcuts by doping, win prize money and if they are caught, they simply pay the fine and continue with their careers. That is not enough to deter offenders or protect the integrity of athletics.” Keter said. Athletics Kenya (AK) Kericho County branch Vice Chairman Gabriel Kiptanui who doubles up as an athletics Coach called for mandatory anti-doping sensitization programs in schools and athletics training camps, saying early education would instill ethical and moral values among athletes and their coaches. He said the initiative would help create a culture of honesty and integrity in the sport while ensuring young athletes understand the consequences of doping early in their careers and carry the message of clean sport as they progress through the ranks. “We should make anti-doping sensitization programs mandatory in schools and athletics training camps. This will instill ethical and moral values among athletes and their coaches, create a culture of honesty and integrity in the sport, and ensure young athletes understand the consequences of doping early in their careers so they can champion clean sport as they rise through the ranks.” said Kiptanui. They recommended greater awareness of Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUEs), saying many athletes still lack adequate knowledge about the process for using prohibited medications legitimately when medically necessary. In an interview with ADAK Principal Education Officer Kennedy Mwai said the public participation forum was intended to gather views from athletes, coaches and other stakeholders on the proposed amendments to the Anti-Doping Act 2016. He said several provisions of the Act require review to align them with the 2027 World Anti-Doping Code, adding that the views collected during the forum will inform the law-making process. Mwai said the World Anti-Doping Code is the global framework that harmonizes the fight against doping in sport and it is reviewed every four years to address emerging challenges and strengthen anti-doping measures. He said the latest edition of the Code has already been adopted by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), requiring all signatories including national anti-doping organizations, to review and amend their domestic laws to align with its provisions. The ADAK officer noted that the proposed amendments to Kenya Anti-Doping Act 2016 are intended to ensure the country’s legal framework remains compliant with the revised World Anti-Doping Code. “Doping is a matter of national concern because of the number of athletes testing positive for prohibited substances. Kenya is a reputable sporting nation and that is why the government is taking the fight against doping very seriously.” Mwai said. Among the areas proposed for amendment are provisions relating to sanctions and penalties for doping offences, anti-doping education and awareness, Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUEs), investigations and results management and other sections aimed at aligning the Anti-Doping Act 2016 with the revised World Anti-Doping Code. The views collected from Kericho athletes, coaches and other relevant stakeholders during the public participation is a constitutional requirement aimed at ensuring citizens contribute to the development of legislation. Currently Kenya is in the category A of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) compliance watch list since 2016 and so far neatly 130 Kenyan athletes mainly long distance runners have been sanctioned for drugs offences since 2017. In June 2024, Kenya handed a life-time ban to marathon runner Beatrice Toroitich and a six year ban to 10km record holder Rhonex Kipruto. By Sarah Njagi

Most Ikuu Boys School candidates meet varsity entry points. By D, KNA Almost all candidates who sat for last year’s Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) at Ikuu Boys High School have qualified for university entry points. With a mean score of 9.2, at least 310 out of the 315 candidates who sat for the national examination met the minimum university threshold of C plus. The national school based in Tharaka-Nithi County has posted an impressive performance. According to the Principal Morris Thigaa, this translates to a remarkable 98.43 percent university transition rate. Speaking to the press at the school, Thigaa attributed the strong results to discipline, hard work, teamwork, and close collaboration among teachers, non-teaching staff, parents, and education stakeholders. The results show that seven candidates scored grade A, 37 attained A-minus, 93 earned B+ (plus), 83 scored B, and 64 managed B-minus. In addition, 26 candidates attained C-plus, while five scored grade C. “This is a good performance and a clear demonstration that when discipline, commitment, and teamwork are embraced, boys can perform exceptionally well,” said Thigaa. He emphasized that the boy child can achieve even greater results if hard work and determination remain central. “I have no doubt that with dedication and focus, our boys can perform even better in future,” he added. The principal highlighted that the school counsels students as they grow, closely following their behavior to ensure discipline. He also spoke about Ikūū for Ikūū, a student-led club that raises funds to support learners who cannot afford school fees, calling it a model of selfless service and solidarity. Thigaa commended the unity between teachers and non-teaching staff, noting that their dedication and shared responsibility played a key role in guiding learners to success. He also thanked parents and other stakeholders for their continued support, emphasizing that collective effort was critical in achieving positive outcomes. He urged students to remain focused and disciplined, encouraging them to maintain the culture of hard work that has defined the school’s academic excellence.

English: Marsabit leaders push for increased ID and voter registration. Marsabit County leaders have raised concern over low voter registration among residents despite ongoing government efforts to increase access to national identity cards (IDs), urging eligible citizens, especially the youth, to register and participate in democratic processes. Led by Governor Mohamud Ali, the leaders said the county has fallen short of its target of registering 300,000 voters over the past four years, attributing the shortfall to apathy, inadequate awareness, and challenges that previously affected access to identity documents. Speaking during a press conference at Jirime Resort in Marsabit town, Governor Ali said the government has streamlined the process of acquiring identity cards after removing vetting requirements and other barriers that had slowed down registration. The press conference was attended by Marsabit County Commissioner Stanley Kamande, Saku MP Dido Raso, North Horr MP Wario Adhe, Laisamis MP Joseph Lekuton, and County Woman Representative Naomi Waqo. Governor Ali emphasized that registration for identity cards remains a free government service and warned chiefs and other administrators against demanding illegal payments from applicants seeking the essential documents. He said reports of residents being asked to pay money before accessing ID registration services should be investigated, noting that such practices could be contributing to the low uptake of registration. The Governor revealed that about 17,000 processed identity cards are currently lying uncollected at registration of persons offices and chiefs’ offices across the county. He urged residents who had applied for the documents to collect them to enable them access government services and participate fully in civic activities. The leaders also expressed concern that approximately 104,000 residents who already possess identity cards have not registered as voters. They called for increased awareness campaigns targeting pastoralist communities, who they said require more information on the importance of voter registration. The registration exercise, being conducted under the 100 Days Rapid Results Initiative (RRI), will also allow holders of old-generation identity cards to apply for the new-generation cards. Laisamis MP Joseph Lekuton called for greater focus on secondary schools, saying thousands of students who have reached the required age should be encouraged to obtain identity cards and register as voters. “We need to focus on our young people in schools because many of them are eligible for ID registration and will later become voters,” Lekuton said. Saku MP Dido Raso attributed the low registration numbers partly to historical challenges where some adults faced difficulties obtaining identity cards due to strict vetting procedures. He said the removal of previous obstacles by the Kenya Kwanza administration had created an opportunity for all eligible Kenyans to access identification documents and participate in national programmes. The leaders urged residents to take advantage of the ongoing exercise and register as voters to exercise their constitutional right to elect leaders of their choice during the General Election. North Horr MP Wario Adhe and Woman Representative Naomi Waqo warned that residents risk being excluded from the electoral process if they fail to register. Waqo noted that women remain behind in the number of registered ID holders and voters and called for deliberate efforts to close the gap. She appealed to men in pastoralist communities to support women by allowing them time away from household and livestock duties to acquire IDs and register as voters. Responding to allegations of illegal charges during ID registration, County Commissioner Stanley Kamande warned government officials and administrators against engaging in corrupt practices. Kamande said unauthorized charges imposed on citizens’ amount to misconduct and assured residents that officers found culpable would face disciplinary action and prosecution where necessary. He urged residents to report any cases of corruption to relevant authorities, saying the government would not tolerate individuals who exploit citizens while providing public services. By Sebastian Miriti and Anthony Melly

Kwale county government joins Mbuguni land case to defend residents’ rights. The Kwale County Government will join an ongoing court case as an interested party to support residents of Mbuguni Settlement Scheme in Tsimba Golini Ward, Matuga Sub-County, who are challenging the alleged unlawful issuance of title deeds. Governor Fatuma Achani announced the move during a public meeting with residents, saying her administration was committed to protecting community land from illegal acquisition and ensuring justice for affected families. The Mbuguni Settlement Scheme comprises approximately 756 plots spread across the villages of Bang’a, Mteza, Mrera, Mbuguni and Lunguma. Residents have raised concerns that title deeds for the land were issued to influential individuals and non-residents, exposing long-time occupants to possible displacement. “My government will join the Mbuguni Scheme case currently before the court as an interested party to ensure that residents receive justice,” said Achani. She reiterated that her administration would not tolerate land grabbing and pledged to work closely with the community’s legal team to reclaim the disputed land. The Governor noted that the county government, in collaboration with institutions such as the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC), had successfully repossessed public land in different parts of the county, including 31 acres on Chale Island in Msambweni Sub-County, land on Kisite Mpunguti Island in Lunga Lunga Sub-County, and a 13-acre parcel in Diani valued at approximately Sh200 million. “These victories demonstrate our commitment to safeguarding public resources and protecting the rights of our people. We shall pursue every legal avenue available to ensure Mbuguni residents are not deprived of their land,” she said. Matuga Member of Parliament Kassim Tandaza backed the Governor’s position, assuring residents that leaders would remain united in defending their rights. “I will not allow residents to be evicted from their land simply because they do not have title deeds. We will stand with them until this matter is resolved,” said Tandaza. Tsimba Golini MCA Mwachuo Mwaboza called on residents to remain calm and allow the judicial process to take its course. “I urge residents not to take the law into their own hands but to maintain peace as the matter is being handled in court,” he said. Residents welcomed the county government’s intervention, expressing optimism that it would help bring an end to the long-standing dispute. Peter Mbovu, one of the residents, said the community had lived on and depended on the land for generations and hoped the legal process would restore their ownership rights. “We appreciate the support from the county government. Our only wish is to see justice prevail and our land returned to its rightful owners,” he said. Another resident, Swaleh Simba, said the community had endured years of uncertainty and thanked local leaders for taking up their cause. “We have suffered for a long time. Today’s commitment by our leaders gives us hope that our children and future generations will continue living on this land,” he said. By Chari Suche

Kiambu Students Receive Bursaries Ahead of School Reopening. Thousands of needy students in Kiambu County are set to start the new school term with financial relief, after Governor Kimani Wamatangi officially launched the distribution of bursary cheques across the county. The exercise, conducted over the weekend in Ndeiya Ward ahead of the school reopening this today, provided thousands of students with financial support of KSh 5,000 for day scholars and KSh 10,000 for boarders in secondary schools. This initiative is part of a revamped county program aimed at ensuring no child is left behind in accessing education. The initiative is part of Governor Wamatangi’s ambitious education support program, which has increased the county’s bursary allocation from Ksh 500 million to Ksh 750 million for the 2025/2026 financial year. Speaking at the ceremony, Governor Wamatangi reiterated his administration’s commitment to promoter the education of the less privileged members of the society and the general development of the education sector. “By expanding the bursary fund, my administration aims to increase the number of beneficiaries and enhance the amount allocated to each student. This substantial increment underscores our commitment to making education accessible to all children in Kiambu County,” said Governor Wamatangi, noting that the expanded allocation would ensure students across all 60 wards benefit from the program. The governor also commended Chief Officer for Education, Gender, Culture and Social Services, Emily Nkoroi, for her dedication in strengthening the department. Unlike previous arrangements where students received one-off support, the enhanced bursary program is structured to provide assistance multiple times throughout the academic year, ensuring sustained support for students. I urge members of the bursary committee to maintain transparency and efficiency in the distribution process. As Kiambu County leadership, we are committed to ensuring that the bursaries reach genuine beneficiaries,” added Deputy Governor Rosemary Kirika. Parents like Mary Wanjiku from Limuru welcomed the initiative. Her daughter received a Shs.h8,000 bursary. “This support has come at the right time when we were struggling to raise school fees. My daughter can now continue her education without interruption,” she said. The distribution exercise is being conducted across all 60 wards, with local administrators working closely with ward education committees to identify deserving beneficiaries. Strict measures have been put in place to ensure transparency and prevent favoritism. The increased funding is expected to benefit over 38,000 students, enabling them to pursue their academic dreams without financial constraints. The timing of the bursary distribution, just before schools reopen, reflects the county’s proactive approach in addressing educational challenges, ensuring students report to school on time and focus on their studies.

NDMA launches an assessment on the impact of the Long rains in Marsabit. The National Drought Management Authority (NDMA) is conducting an impact assessment exercise on the recent long rains which was largely inadequate in most parts of Marsabit County. The assessment follows a review meeting on the effect of the March-May rain season on food, nutrition and security by the county steering group (CSG. NDMA County Coordinator Guyo Golicha pointed out that checklists presented by the various technical departments that include agriculture, education, health, livestock, security and water save for peace and security had painted a picture of inadequacy because the rains were not sufficient. Golicha said the exercise which is normally conducted after every rain season in ASAL regions by the authority was aimed at providing the actual picture on the ground in terms of food and nutrition, availability of grazing resources and whether the situation poses any threat to peace. Apart from the agro-pastoralist areas of Moyale and Saku sub-counties which received some considerable amount of rainfall, the rest of the county remained dry. The County Coordinator added that the information gathered by the two teams that will cover all the 20 wards in the county will help in assessing the impact that the March-April- May rains had on livelihoods of local pastoralist communities. “We want to know what impact the rains we received have had on our people and their livelihoods and how it affected the different sectors,” he said. Golicha pointed out that the evaluation that will take five days will in particular pay attention to livestock and pasture which are critical to the local economy and the survival of almost all households. He said approximately 82.3 per cent of the population depends on livestock for their livelihood, making the sector a key pointer to the county’s recovery from drought with the assessment teams focusing more on milk production and performance of livestock markets. The body condition of livestock, the availability of pasture and the status of water sources like dams, pans, boreholes, the availability of food stuffs and their prices will also be assessed. The drought coordinator added that the distance communities travel to access water and migration of livestock would also be of interest to the evaluators because long distances often affect the health of both humans and livestock as well as productivity. “When livestock travel long distances to access water their body conditions deteriorate. The closer the water is, the better it is for the animals, “he said. The outcome of the assessment would enable the government and other stakeholders to plan for interventions to ensure that the necessary assistance to those afflicted by drought is available on time. “Water is one of the major areas of concern in Marsabit County. We want to establish the current levels of water so that we can focus our efforts on zones that need support most,” Golicha said The exercise is also set to come up with recommendations on how to prepare the county for the El-Nino which is anticipated later in the year. Golicha observed that while enhanced rains have positive gains for communities and their economic mainstay- livestock, excessive water could wreak havoc and generate health challenges if not properly managed. He said the exercise would rely on a checklist provided by the various technical departments in collecting data that would inform on the appropriate mitigation measures against the climate shocks. By Sebastian Miriti and Anthony Melly

English: Government to fast-track completion of Chebara education projects. The Government has reaffirmed its commitment to fast-track the completion of stalled education infrastructure projects in Chebara, Elgeyo Marakwet County, as part of a nationwide programme to revive incomplete public investments and maximise returns on public expenditure. Interior and National Administration Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen made the commitment during an inspection of education facilities relocated to pave the way for the Chebara Dam Project but which have remained incomplete for more than a decade. Murkomen said the Kenya Kwanza Administration had prioritised the completion of stalled capital projects to improve public service delivery, optimise infrastructure use and safeguard public investment. “The Kenya Kwanza Administration is firmly committed to completing all stalled projects across the country to unlock their socio-economic benefits and deliver value for resources invested,” he said. The Cabinet Secretary toured the stalled Chebara Vocational Training Centre, Chebara Boys High School, AIC Chebara Girls High School, Chebara Comprehensive School and AIC Chebara Chapel, all relocated under the Chebara Dam Resettlement Programme. He said delays were occasioned by the non-performance of the initial contractor, leaving the facilities unfinished and affecting learning for communities displaced by the dam project. Murkomen noted that the prolonged suspension of the projects had limited access to quality education, technical and vocational training and other essential social services in the area. He said the Government would implement a Presidential directive to mobilise the required resources, complete procurement for a replacement contractor and accelerate construction in line with approved engineering standards and contractual requirements. “We will ensure full implementation of the Presidential directive to mobilise resources and fast-track the work of the new contractor following the previous contractor’s failure to complete the projects,” he said. During the inspection, Murkomen reviewed the progress of the stalled facilities and directed implementing agencies to strengthen project supervision, contract management and inter-agency coordination to ensure timely completion and adherence to quality standards. The Cabinet Secretary later visited Tambach Teachers Training College, where he inspected the ongoing rehabilitation of academic infrastructure and construction of additional student hostels. He said expanding the institution’s capacity would strengthen teacher training and improve the quality of education. Murkomen also assessed the proposed site for Kerio University, describing the planned institution as a strategic investment that will expand access to university education, research, innovation and skills development in the region. Local leaders welcomed the Government’s renewed commitment, saying completion of the projects would restore learning services disrupted by the Chebara Dam development, increase access to technical and higher education and spur socio-economic growth. The inspection is part of the Government’s national monitoring and evaluation programme for stalled public infrastructure projects aimed at improving project governance, enhancing accountability in public resource utilisation and accelerating implementation of priority development programmes under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA). By Rennish Okong’o

MPs rally Teso North residents behind Ruto’s 2027 re-election bid. A section of Members of Parliament has urged residents of Teso North Constituency to support President William Ruto’s re-election in the 2027 General Election, citing the Kenya Kwanza administration’s development record and ongoing economic empowerment programmes. The leaders made the appeal during a women’s economic empowerment programme held at Kakemer in Teso North Constituency, where funds were raised to boost working capital for women-owned small businesses. The event brought together Ugenya MP David Ochieng’, Teso North MP Oku Kaunya and Teso South MP Mary Emase, who called on residents to continue supporting the government’s development agenda. Addressing participants, Ochieng’ said the government had made significant progress over the past three years in infrastructure development, education, job creation and economic empowerment. He urged voters to grant President Ruto a second term, arguing that continuity in leadership would enable the government to complete ongoing projects and fully implement its development programmes. “We cannot elect leaders without a clear plan for the country. President Ruto has outlined his agenda and has already demonstrated commitment to supporting the youth, women, education, roads, industries and job creation,” said Ochieng’. He also appealed for peaceful political competition ahead of the 2027 elections, urging leaders across the political divide to conduct campaigns without violence, intimidation or incitement. “Let us compete peacefully and avoid using violence or hiring goons to disrupt political activities. Young people should reject attempts by politicians to use them to cause chaos or intimidate opponents,” he said. Teso South MP Mary Emase called for issue-based politics, urging leaders to prioritise development and initiatives that improve the livelihoods of wananchi instead of engaging in divisive politics. She also commended the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) for what she described as its credible management of the recently concluded by-elections. Teso North MP Oku Kaunya urged leaders to strengthen economic empowerment initiatives targeting women and youth, saying increased access to income-generating opportunities would improve household incomes, create jobs and promote sustainable socio-economic development in the constituency. By Moses Wekesa

Deaf youth in Vihiga embrace enterprise fund opportunities. Hearing-impaired youth in Vihiga County have been encouraged to take advantage of government financing programmes to grow businesses, improve livelihoods and achieve economic independence. The call was made during an empowerment forum organised by the Youth Enterprise Development Fund (YEDF) at Gambogi Fellowship Centre grounds, where members of the Hamisi hearing-impaired group were sensitized on access to affordable credit, group formation requirements and financial management. The forum brought together 12 members of the group, who have been working collectively through income-generating activities aimed at improving their economic wellbeing despite challenges associated with disability and limited access to financial opportunities. Speaking during the engagement, Vihiga County Youth Fund Credit Officer Cleophas Odhiambo Omanya said the Fund is committed to ensuring that marginalised groups, including persons living with disabilities, benefit from government empowerment programmes. Omanya said registered youth groups can access loans starting from Sh100,000, with opportunities to qualify for higher amounts depending on their repayment record. He explained that the funds are designed to support small enterprises, including retail businesses, agribusiness ventures and service-related activities, enabling young people to create sustainable sources of income. “We want every young person, including those living with disabilities, to understand that they can access financial support to improve their lives and contribute to economic development,” Omanya said. Assistant County Credit Officer William Osundwa urged members of the group to maintain unity, trust and accountability, noting that collective responsibility is essential for the success of funded enterprises. Osundwa revealed that the Hamisi hearing-impaired group had demonstrated strong financial discipline after successfully repaying their first loan of Sh100,000 per member within one year. He said the achievement had qualified the members to access a second loan of Sh200,000 each, payable within 18 months through a structured repayment plan of Sh11,200 monthly. The payments, he added, are made through the government’s e-Citizen platform to enhance transparency and accountability in loan management. Osundwa further noted that beyond financial support, the Youth Enterprise Development Fund provides beneficiaries with mentorship and entrepreneurship training to strengthen their skills in business planning, financial management and investment decisions. The empowerment session was conducted through sign language interpretation by Nicholas Ogango, allowing participants to fully engage in discussions and seek clarification on various aspects of the programme. Hamisi Hearing-Impaired Group Vice Chairperson Derrick Mahaya said the initiative had opened opportunities for members who previously faced difficulties accessing capital due to communication barriers and limited information about available support programmes. Mahaya said the group had embraced table banking and collective saving, enabling members to establish small businesses such as vending and retail enterprises. “We have come from far. Many of us had ideas but lacked capital. With this support, we will grow our businesses, support our families and become financially independent,” he said. He appealed to stakeholders to continue developing inclusive financial products and capacity-building programmes tailored to the needs of persons living with disabilities. Members of the group highlighted challenges including limited access to capital, communication barriers and inadequate exposure to business opportunities. However, they expressed optimism that continued support from the Youth Enterprise Development Fund would help them expand their ventures and improve their living standards. The officials also guided participants on loan application procedures, including group registration, proposal writing, savings requirements and responsible borrowing practices. The forum marks a step towards strengthening economic inclusion for hearing-impaired youth in Vihiga County as the government continues to promote programmes aimed at reducing unemployment, encouraging entrepreneurship and enhancing financial independence among young people. By Crispinus Ivan

Turkana pastoralists welcome mass livestock vaccination drive to Combat Diseases. Livestock keepers in Elelea Ward, Turkana East Sub-County, have welcomed a mass livestock vaccination and supportive treatment campaign aimed at improving animal health, controlling diseases and expanding access to domestic and international livestock markets. The 10-day exercise, being implemented through a partnership between the Turkana County Government and GENCO Livestock and Fresh Meat Export Ltd, targets the vaccination and treatment of more than 100,000 animals in Elelea, Karoge and Lokapel. The campaign focuses on protecting livestock against Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR), a highly contagious viral disease affecting sheep and goats, as well as other common livestock diseases. Kamar Lojao, a livestock keeper from Echoke Village, said the exercise would help reduce livestock losses caused by disease outbreaks and improve household incomes that depend on livestock production. Community Disease Reporter (CDR) Ngitira Ekitela said PPR and tick-borne diseases remain the most common livestock diseases in Elelea and neighbouring areas. While welcoming the vaccination programme, Ekitela appealed to the County Government to provide acaricides to help pastoralists control tick infestations and further improve livestock health. During a supervision visit, the Director of Veterinary Services, Dr Benson Long’or, said the campaign had made significant progress, with more than 30,000 animals vaccinated and treated within the first three days. “We have vaccinated and treated over 30,000 animals in Elelea and Lokapel within three days. With the continued cooperation of livestock keepers, we expect to surpass our target of 100,000 animals by the end of the campaign,” said Dr Long’or. He said the vaccination and supportive treatment programme is designed to produce disease-free animals at the farm gate, enabling pastoralists to access premium local and export markets while strengthening the livestock value chain. Dr Long’or added that the County Government had provided vaccines, dewormers, veterinary equipment and technical personnel to ensure the success of the campaign. The exercise follows a consultative meeting held in Lodwar between officials from the County Department of Livestock and GENCO Livestock and Fresh Meat Export Ltd to strengthen livestock disease control initiatives in Turkana. GENCO veterinarian Dr Sibiah Ratemo praised the commitment of county veterinary officers and community mobilisers, saying the partnership had attracted a high turnout of pastoralists at designated vaccination points. He also commended women for their role in mobilising communities and encouraged their increased participation in future livestock health campaigns to improve outreach and disease control efforts. By Peter Gitonga

English: Senator calls for crackdown on political goonism ahead of elections. Nakuru Senator and Deputy Majority Leader Tabitha Karanja has called on security agencies to dismantle organised political goonism, warning that rising cases of violence and intimidation could undermine Kenya’s democracy and peaceful campaigns ahead of the 2027 General Election. Speaking during an engagement with opinion leaders at her Naivasha residence, Karanja said incidents of violence witnessed during church events, political rallies and campaigns had continued to increase despite government assurances that perpetrators would face legal action. Her remarks come after the Ol Kalou by-election, where reports of violence, intimidation and disruption attracted condemnation from leaders across the political divide. During the election exercise, rival supporters reportedly clashed in several areas, leaving some people injured, while journalists covering the poll said they were harassed by suspected goons. Karanja alleged that individuals involved in the chaos had planned their actions in advance and that their identities were already known. She urged security agencies to take decisive action against those behind political violence, saying failure to act could encourage criminal groups and weaken public confidence in democratic institutions. “I urge Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen and Inspector-General of Police Douglas Kanja to be honest with Kenyans and arrest these criminals once and for all because they are well known to the people,” she said. The senator warned that continued political violence could also affect the economy by discouraging investors and creating uncertainty, undermining efforts to build a stable environment for businesses. She said leaders sponsoring violence risked damaging the country’s reputation and threatening the government’s commitment to promoting economic growth. Karanja also attributed the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) party’s defeat in the Ol Kalou by-election to what she described as arrogance and excessive confidence among some leaders within the party. She claimed that despite heavy investment in the campaign, voters rejected the party’s candidate because of what she termed as displays of arrogance, violence and offensive political rhetoric. “It is time the President reconstituted his inner circle because the current one is tarnishing his name and is responsible for the loss in Ol Kalou,” she said. Karanja warned that the party’s image was being damaged and could lead some leaders to consider shifting allegiance ahead of the next General Election. She accused some politicians of promoting vote buying, intimidation and divisive politics instead of engaging voters through meaningful discussions on development issues. The senator condemned alleged harassment of journalists during the Ol Kalou by-election, saying media practitioners play a critical role in informing the public and should be allowed to carry out their duties without interference. She said attacks against journalists undermine constitutional guarantees on media freedom and weaken accountability during electoral processes. Karanja further criticized the use of young people to perpetrate violence during political activities, saying youths should instead be empowered through employment opportunities, skills development and economic support. By Erastus Gichohi and Beatrice Wanjiku

Kirinyaga trains 2,000 farmers on high-yield maize varieties. More than 2,000 farmers in Kirinyaga County have been trained on high-yielding maize varieties under a county government programme aimed at increasing maize production, strengthening dairy farming and preparing farmers to take advantage of the anticipated El Niño rains. The training, conducted in partnership with Bayer East Africa Limited, equipped farmers with practical knowledge on selecting maize varieties suited to different ecological zones and planting seasons, climate-smart farming practices and available market opportunities to improve productivity and household incomes. The initiative is being implemented under Governor Anne Waiguru’s Masomo Mkulima Mashinani programme, which delivers agricultural extension and advisory services directly to farmers across the county. Speaking during the training, Governor Waiguru said the programme enables extension officers to conduct practical demonstrations on crop and livestock value chains, helping farmers adopt modern technologies that enhance productivity, resilience and profitability. “This support is part of the Wezesha Kirinyaga programme, which seeks to transform the lives of smallholder farmers by supporting households engaged in various agricultural value chains to increase production and access better markets,” she said. Waiguru said the county government would continue investing in value addition, post-harvest handling and market access to protect farmers from price fluctuations and exploitation by middlemen. “Our next phase is about sustainability, ensuring every farmer continues to grow their income and every village becomes part of Kirinyaga’s agricultural success story,” she added. During the training, farmers were introduced to improved maize varieties, including DK777, DK8031, DKC8033, DKC9089 and the newly promoted DK7500, a yellow maize variety recommended for both grain production and silage to support dairy farming. County Executive Committee Member for Agriculture Dr. John Gachara said the programme is supported by 147 agricultural extension officers deployed across all sub-locations to provide technical support, monitor crop performance and collect field data to strengthen extension services. He said similar training programmes are being rolled out across other agricultural value chains to improve productivity and increase farm incomes. Dr. Gachara explained that the county introduced the Masomo Mkulima Mashinani programme after realising that many farmers were unable to travel to the Agricultural Technical and Vocational Education and Training (ATVET) Centre at Kamweti in Karumandi Ward for training. To bridge that gap, the county established the Kangai Tomato Propagation Centre as an extension of the Kamweti facility, enabling farmers to access practical training closer to their homes. He said the county remains committed to ensuring farmers have access to quality seed, practical knowledge and reliable markets, noting that the partnership with Bayer has enabled farmers to learn about improved seed varieties while the county works to expand market opportunities. Dr. Gachara added that the county is monitoring maize performance across different ecological zones to determine the suitability of various seed varieties and farming practices. The findings will guide future extension services and help farmers make informed production decisions. Bayer East Africa trainer Peter Kibure said the training was designed to help farmers understand the characteristics of different maize varieties and select seed best suited to prevailing weather conditions and intended use. He said farmers were introduced to DK7500, a high-yielding yellow maize variety containing about 12 percent protein, making it suitable for both grain production and silage for dairy cattle. The variety also contains beta-carotene and has demonstrated strong performance under favourable rainfall conditions. Kibure said the anticipated El Niño rains present an opportunity for farmers to maximise production by planting varieties that perform well under wetter conditions. Farmers who attended the training welcomed the initiative, saying it had equipped them with practical skills to improve production and increase incomes. Christopher Wanjohi said the programme had provided valuable knowledge that would enable farmers to achieve higher yields and improve their livelihoods. Jane Wambui of Kerugoya Ward said the county’s agricultural training programmes had transformed her maize farming since 2022 by helping her adopt improved seed varieties with better yields. She said she had previously planted low-performing maize varieties but had recorded better harvests after switching to recommended seeds and expressed confidence that the newly introduced DK7500 would further improve maize production across the county. By Mutai Kipng’etich

Kemei urges hospital deliveries to reduce infant mortality. Kericho Woman Representative Beatrice Kemei has called on expectant mothers to embrace hospital deliveries, saying access to skilled birth attendants remains one of the most effective ways of reducing infant mortality and safeguarding the health of both mothers and newborns. Speaking during a funeral service at Kericho Golf Club, Kemei said although Kenya has made significant progress in reducing child mortality, preventable deaths during childbirth continue to occur because some mothers delay seeking medical care or opt for home deliveries. She noted that many childbirth-related complications can be effectively managed in well-equipped health facilities where skilled healthcare professionals, emergency obstetric services and newborn care are readily available. “We want to get rid of infant mortality. Let us improve our hospitals and encourage women to give birth in hospitals. We still have cases where complications during childbirth claim the lives of babies, yet many of these deaths can be prevented through skilled care,” said Kemei. She observed that hospital deliveries guarantee access to qualified medical personnel who can provide emergency obstetric care, newborn resuscitation, postnatal monitoring and timely referrals whenever complications arise. The Woman Representative also called for continued investment in maternity infrastructure, adequate medical equipment and the recruitment of skilled healthcare workers to strengthen maternal and newborn healthcare services across Kericho County. Kemei said protecting the lives of mothers and newborns requires collective responsibility, urging families and communities to support expectant mothers throughout pregnancy by encouraging regular antenatal clinic attendance and ensuring they deliver in health facilities. Kericho County has continued to register steady improvements in maternal and child health, reflecting sustained government investment in healthcare services. According to the latest Kenya National Bureau of Statistics County Statistical Abstract, the county’s infant mortality rate stands at 25 deaths per 1,000 live births, compared to 37.8 deaths per 1,000 live births recorded in earlier estimates. The county also reports an under-five mortality rate of 32 deaths per 1,000 live births, placing it below the national average. The gains have been attributed to expanded antenatal and postnatal care services, increased uptake of skilled birth attendance, improved immunisation coverage and strengthened community health programmes. Data from the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey indicates that most births in Kericho are attended by skilled health providers, while childhood immunisation coverage remains among the highest in the country, contributing to improved survival rates for infants and young children. Despite the progress, health experts caution that the neonatal period—the first month after birth—remains the most vulnerable stage for newborn survival. Premature birth, birth asphyxia, infections and delayed access to emergency obstetric care continue to account for a significant proportion of infant deaths, underscoring the need for expectant mothers to seek skilled medical care throughout pregnancy and during delivery. Kemei stressed that eliminating preventable infant deaths will require close collaboration between government, healthcare providers, communities and families to ensure pregnant women receive quality maternal healthcare services. She said sustained public awareness campaigns, improved healthcare infrastructure and increased access to skilled birth attendants will play a critical role in improving maternal and child health outcomes. The government’s continued investment in modern maternity facilities, expansion of community health services, recruitment of skilled healthcare workers and implementation of the Social Health Authority is expected to further strengthen maternal and newborn healthcare in Kericho County. As Kenya works towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals on maternal and child survival by 2030, health stakeholders continue to encourage expectant mothers to utilise antenatal services and deliver in health facilities to give every child a healthier start to life. By Gilbert Mutai

English: Government unveils historic health disability policy. The Ministry of Health has officially launched the Health Sector Disability Mainstreaming Policy to ensure that all healthcare facilities across the country are fully inclusive and accessible to persons with disabilities (PWDs). The policy, which has been under development for over six years, targets physical, institutional, and attitudinal barriers within public, private, and faith-based healthcare facilities. Speaking during the launch in Nairobi, Principal Secretary for the State Department for Public Health and Professional Standards, Mary Muthoni, emphasized that disability mainstreaming was a fundamental commitment to human dignity rather than a mere policy narrative. “For too long, the narrative around disability has been one of limitation,” PS Muthoni stated. “Today, by integrating disability perspectives directly into our health system, we are decisively shifting that narrative. We are moving away from exclusionary models towards a system that guarantees equitable access for all Kenyans.” To ensure immediate execution, the ministry fast-tracked both the policy and its operational guidelines simultaneously. “We are not going to have it sit on the shelves waiting for implementation guidelines,” Muthoni said, adding, “We want to hit the ground running.” Ministry of Health’s Head of Rehabilitative Services Ms. Irene Gichohi called for immediate compliance across all healthcare sectors. “The idea is that, from the very beginning, we should design services, infrastructure, and equipment that are universally accessible,” she said, stressing that institutions should avoid relying on makeshift, retrofitted adjustments after facilities are built. Gichohi welcomed the collaboration that made the document’s launch possible after a long six-year journey. Following Gichohi’s remarks, the government highlighted its plans to integrate Community Health Promoters (CHPs) to identify, assess, and refer PWDs within their neighborhoods. Muthoni revealed that plans are underway to incorporate disability mainstreaming into the CHP training curriculum. “It is not just about identification of who is unwell or who is disabled,” the PS explained. “It is equally an opportunity to ensure that we prevent disability from happening, right from conception.” Representing the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD), Senior Disability Services Officer Mr. Isaac Manyonge highlighted the everyday hurdles PWDs face, ranging from inaccessible registration desks to a lack of sign language interpreters in hospitals. “Article 54 of our Constitution speaks about the right of a person with a disability to access institutions and the facilities within them.” Manyonge noted, explaining, “It is one thing to access an institution, and it is another to access the actual facilities inside.” Manyonge emphasized the need for disability etiquette among healthcare providers, noting that medical professionals must understand that PWDs require equal respect and dignified care. He added that the policy also seeks to leverage CHPs to collect reliable demographic data, which will help reform medical procurement to include disability-specific treatments and assistive devices. Under the Social Health Authority (SHA), the government is tailoring specific benefit packages to cover essential assistive devices and rehabilitative services. PS Muthoni also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to enforcing a two percent public procurement quota specifically for PWD-owned enterprises. “Disability is a club that anyone can join at any time of life,” Manyonge said. “This policy is about all of us, protecting those who have disabilities today, and those who may acquire them tomorrow.” By Lilian Gichohi

Mutula Care offers hope to vulnerable families. The County Government of Makueni has launched a comprehensive health care initiative to cover at least 11,000 vulnerable households under the Universal Health Care (UHC) programme. The initiative dubbed Mutula Care and spearheaded by Makueni Governor Mutula Kilonzo Jr. intends to accommodate all the less fortunate members of the society in the county under the universal health cover. The launch was done by the County Executive Committee Member for Health Joyce Mutua at Wote Town Multi-Purpose Hall, Green Park in Makueni Subcounty on Thursday. Ms. Mutua disclosed that they had already registered 10,100 vulnerable families and paid annual Social Insurance premiums. She assured 1,000 households whose names were wrongly captured that they will be included in the programme adding the County government intended to increase the beneficiaries to 25,000 in due course. “We did target jointly with the community to identify the most vulnerable households. The government has paid annual premiums ranging between Sh3,600 and Sh15,000 per family. The insurance runs up to May, 2027, when it will be renewed,” she told the media. The CECM explained that the beneficiaries through the scheme will access outpatient and inpatient services at all public health facilities up to referral hospitals besides getting packaged maternity services, renal treatment, and mental health among other health care services provided under Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF). She said previously the government used to do a lot of waivers to vulnerable families who were unable to pay for hospital bills. “Earlier, the government made waivers of huge amounts of money for patients who could not afford to pay for the services,” she said, adding that by ensuring payment for their insurance in advance, these needy patients will access health care without any hindrance. Mutua further said that each of the registered households will have parents and their dependents below 18 years covered and urged needy residents in the county to enroll in the scheme. She said free ambulance referral services took effect on July 1, 2026, explaining that patients referred to distant hospitals, including Kenyatta National Hospital and Kijabe Hospital, will be transported free of charge to lessen medication costs. By Patrick Nyakundi

English: Directorate reviews of public- private partnerships policy. The Directorate of Public-Private Partnerships (PPP), domiciled at the National Treasury and Economic Planning, has kicked off public participation forums to ensure community engagement, transparency, and stakeholder buy-in of its activities. The PPP Directorate is the technical arm of the PPP Committee at the National Treasury, mandated to facilitate, structure and manage infrastructure and development projects between the public and private sectors. Director General (DG) of the PPP Eng. Kefa Seda says that the forums provide a platform for citizens and stakeholders to review the legal instruments and submit their views before their finalization. Eng. Seda said the nationwide public participation forums on the review of the PPP legal framework are officially underway. He said the consultative sessions that began on the 13th of July, 2026, run until July 29, 2026, and provide citizens and stakeholders an opportunity to review proposed amendments aimed at streamlining project procurement, enhancing transparency, and clarifying county government roles in PPP investments. The PPP DG said the public consultations cover the draft PPP (Amendment) Bill, 2026, and associated management regulations. The DG reaffirmed the government’s commitment to addressing the country’s huge infrastructure deficit through stronger collaboration with the private sector under the PPP initiatives. He said the objective of the public forums, besides fulfilling the requirements of the Constitution, was to accord an opportunity for citizens and stakeholders to review the PPP legal instruments and submit their views before finalization and submission to Parliament. Eng. Seda spoke to the press at the Kenya School of Government (KSG) Mombasa campus during a stakeholders and public participation forum. The Mombasa forum was attended by relevant public and private sector stakeholders drawn from Mombasa, Kilifi, Lamu and Tana River counties. One of the major PPP projects in the coastal region is the Sh. 12.5 billion Galana-Kulalu Food Security project. The Galana-Kulalu Food Security Project, which straddles Kilifi and Tana River counties, brings over 20,000 acres under production and is Kenya’s largest irrigation-based agricultural scheme. “We are calling on the citizens to join the public participation forums taking place across the country and share their views to help shape our PPP legal and regulatory framework,” said Seda. He added: ‘The participation and voice of all citizens matters and counts.’ Eng. Seda said PPPs are essential for funding mega projects because they relieve immense fiscal strain on national budgets while ‘’leveraging private sector expertise, innovation and efficiency. The PPP top official said by transferring financial and operational risks to private entities, the governments can deliver critical infrastructure like highways and energy grids faster and more efficiently. Eng. Seda said the world over, governments and development institutions heavily utilize the PPP model to bridge infrastructure funding gaps. “The PPP funding model remains a viable option to the country’s budgetary constraints,” he said, further underscoring the importance of collaboration between public and private sector players in advancing quality infrastructure development and driving sustainable economic growth. He said typically in PPP arrangements, the government and a private partner enter into a long-term contract to finance public assets that people often need in the infrastructure sector. “The PPP model allows the government to leverage private sector expertise and resources while minimizing financial risks and keeping costs down,” he said. Eng. Seda emphasized that the infrastructure sector is highly resource-intensive and requires massive capital which the government alone can’t handle since they place severe pressure on national budgets and public debt. KFS opens Sh75 million centre to boost forest conservation. The Kenya Forest Service (KFS) has opened a Sh75 million GreenZones Development Support Project II Resource Centre at its headquarters in Nairobi, strengthening efforts to enhance forest conservation, institutional development and environmental sustainability. The facility, funded by the African Development Bank (AfDB), was officially commissioned on Tuesday by Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF) Alex Lemarkoko during a ceremony attended by government officials, development partners and faith leaders led by Africa Inland Church (AIC) Presiding Bishop Rt. Rev. Abraham Mulwa. Lemarkoko said the resource centre comes at a critical time when KFS is undergoing significant transformation through increased staffing, improved ranger training and expanded responsibilities in forest management and restoration. “Kenya Forest Service is undergoing an extremely unique period,” said Lemarkoko, noting that the institution’s workforce has grown from about 3,000 to more than 6,000 employees. He said the increased workforce has been accompanied by improved ranger training and recruitment of technical officers and cadets to strengthen the country’s capacity in managing forest resources. The CCF said KFS is leading efforts to achieve Kenya’s national target of attaining 30 per cent tree cover by 2032 through expansion of tree nurseries and production of quality seedlings for restoration programmes across the country. He added that the agency has strengthened partnerships with government institutions, development organisations and communities to accelerate forest restoration and promote sustainable environmental conservation. Lemarkoko commended the African Development Bank for supporting infrastructure development, forest restoration initiatives and livelihood programmes targeting communities living near forests. He said the partnership has contributed to improved conservation outcomes while supporting household incomes among communities dependent on forest ecosystems. The CCF also announced that KFS is finalising a Memorandum of Understanding with the African Inland Church to provide chaplaincy services for staff, saying the partnership will enhance employee welfare and support the institution’s conservation mandate. He urged Kenyans, especially young people, to embrace tree growing and understand the importance of protecting forests for current and future generations. “We have agreed to plant trees across the country because our young people must understand why we grow trees, how they benefit from them and the role they play in conserving the environment,” he said. AIC Presiding Bishop Rt. Rev. Abraham Mulwa challenged KFS to strengthen public awareness campaigns on forest conservation, saying access to information is essential in encouraging communities to protect natural resources. “Please give people the opportunity to understand how to protect, keep and maintain our forests. When information is shared, people become part of the solution,” Mulwa said. The bishop encouraged Kenyans to protect trees and the environment, noting that forests play a vital role in supporting human health, biodiversity conservation and climate resilience. The commissioning of the facility also marked the dedication of the new resource centre, which replaced an earlier building that was destroyed by fire three years ago. KFS Commander Mohamed Adam Mohamed thanked the government, AfDB and KFS management for supporting the reconstruction of the facility, saying it would serve as an important centre for staff training, environmental education and conservation programmes. He said the centre would enhance the capacity of KFS officers while providing a platform for knowledge sharing and strengthening forest management initiatives. The opening of the resource centre comes ahead of the International Day for the Conservation of the Mangrove Ecosystem, with KFS renewing its call for Kenyans to plant and protect trees across all ecosystems. Kakamega opts for low-cost climate smart agriculture. An international non-governmental organization, Ripple Effect, is encouraging farmers in Kakamega County to embrace agro-ecology, sustainable and climate-smart agriculture to lower production costs and boost yields and soil fertility. During a smallholder farmers’ field day held at Emathayi, organized by Ripple Effect in collaboration with Vivamos, a Swiss organization and the Kenya National Farmers Federation (KENAFF), farmers learned practical and easy-to-access technologies to improve food security, restore soil health and support the transformation of rural livelihoods. Farmers, agricultural experts and agricultural officials attended the event where live demonstrations were conducted on making suitable homemade organic fertilizers, making keyhole gardens, fertility trenches, preservation of indigenous seeds, bee farming, and making of Black Soldier Fly larvae as inexpensive manure for poultry industries. Speaking at the event, the Kakamega County Executive Committee Member for Agriculture, Mophat Mandela, said the County is encouraging farmers to practice climate-smart agriculture to lower production costs for farmers and boost soil fertility and yields. “Overdependence on costly farm inputs has become a serious load to many farmers; locally made organic fertilizers with biodegradable waste is a sustainable alternative,” he added. He highlighted the fact that the soils in the county are facing acidity and low levels of essential nutrients in the soil but added that these new techniques are improving because the farmers have adopted homemade fertilizers and commercial farming. “While agricultural production continued to improve substantially in the past decade, more measures are needed to attain food security and improve farmers’ incomes,” he added. Mandela suggested that farmers integrate the application of both organic and conventional fertilizers, as needed, to increase soil fertility and promote budding agripreneurs to lend a helping hand to fellow farmers by organizing peer-to-peer learning opportunities. He said the county has employed extension officers in all the wards and sub-counties to serve their best interests, also urging them to collaborate more with the farmers for improved agricultural production. Ripple Effect Country Manager Isaac Ogutu said the organization was promoting agro-ecological farming, which was centered on providing higher output in order to sustain the environment for posterity. “The farmers should put into practice the knowledge they have learnt on the field day and transfer their knowledge to people around them to help more farmers understand the sustainable agriculture techniques and practice them,” Ogutu stated. He also urged farmers to grow and conserve their original seeds, which are more resistant to climate changes, pests, diseases, and were better keepers of food and income. “Ripple Effect would increase farmer groups in order to have wide access to training and support systems based on the community,” Ogutu revealed. Habakuk Khamala, a representative of the KENAF, urged farmers to embrace new technologies in the farming process and indigenous farming, particularly technologies like keyhole gardens, fertility trenches that play a big role in crop production amidst changing climate conditions. “Farmers should embrace modern methods even when farming indigenous breeds,” Khamala said. Peer farmer trainer Reuben Malinja demonstrated how Black Soldier Fly larvae can be raised to feed low-cost chickens and farmers can optimally make use of organic waste in chicken farming, which would improve the profitability of the farms. “Farmers should join SACCOs and self-help groups and avail themselves for training, financing and modern farming technologies,” Benjamin Maina urged farmers. Maina also spoke about the economic and medicinal importance of beekeeping. Apart from the production of honey, the bees also generate an extra source of income to the rural households as they generate wax which would be utilized for the making of candles apart from other cottage industries. Another peer farmer trainer, Evelyne Karakacha, exhibited successful production of local vegetables such as cowpea leaves and jute mallow with home-grown organic fertilizers. “The farming of local vegetables using organic fertilizers has increased my productivity, while also lowering production costs,” Evelyne said. Another beneficiary, Esther Osimbo, said she transitioned from hardship to self-reliance after embracing the new farming techniques. “By learning and picking up the skills, I can now produce food, care for my husband who has a disability, and educate my children; this was something I had not been able to do before the training,” Osimbo said The programme has also enabled her to train other farmers, showcasing the far-reaching potential of knowledge transfer to boost opportunities and strengthen livelihoods in entire communities, she said. The field day climaxed with a renewed appeal to farmers to join farmers’ groups and encouraged them to accept climate-smart agriculture and adapt low-cost sustainable technology that can help create resilient farms for improved household income and long-term food security. By Paul Nyokech

English: Modern ECDE centres transform learning in Lugari. For years, many children in Lugari Sub-County began their education in overcrowded classrooms with leaking roofs, inadequate learning materials and poor sanitation facilities. Today, that picture is gradually changing as the County Government of Kakamega continues investing in modern Early Childhood Development Education (ECDE) centres aimed at giving young learners a strong foundation. The transformation is evident at Munyuki Primary School in Lumakanda Ward, where a newly commissioned ECDE centre now offers spacious classrooms, a kitchen, clean water, modern sanitation facilities and a safe environment designed for children. The facility is among more than 61 ECDE centres that the county government is constructing across Kakamega County to improve access to quality early childhood education. Parents say the improved infrastructure has renewed confidence in public ECDE centres. Mary Naliaka, a parent from Lumakanda, says the new classrooms have greatly improved the learning environment for young children. “Previously our children were learning in old classrooms that became muddy whenever it rained. Today they have a clean, secure and child-friendly environment. We no longer worry about their safety because they are learning in classrooms that are suitable for their age,” she said. Peter Wekesa, another parent, says the county’s investment has encouraged more parents to enroll their children in public ECDE centres. “Many parents who previously preferred private nursery schools are now bringing their children here because the facilities have greatly improved. The classrooms are bright, the furniture is suitable for young learners and there is clean water. Our children are excited to attend school every day,” he said. The improved infrastructure is also translating into increased enrolment in public ECDE centres and in addition to improved learning facilities, school feeding programmes are enhancing learner attendance and retention. Education stakeholders say proper nutrition has become an important complement to the county’s investment in quality infrastructure, as well-fed learners are more likely to attend school consistently and perform better academically. A teacher at Munyuki Primary School says enrollment at the school’s ECDE section has continued to rise since the completion of the new classrooms, adding that better infrastructure and the availability of school meals have also improved attendance, learner participation and classroom interaction, making it easier to implement the Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC). County Executive Committee Member for Education, Science and Technology, Dr. Bernard Amwayi, says the county is constructing modern classrooms, providing age-appropriate furniture, improving sanitation facilities, and ensuring access to clean water besides recruiting qualified ECDE teachers to enhance the quality of early learning. “Our objective is to ensure every child begins school in a safe, stimulating and conducive learning environment. We believe quality education starts with quality infrastructure, competent teachers, adequate learning resources and proper nutrition,” noted Dr. Amwayi. He said the county continues to strengthen school feeding initiatives in ECDE centres because good nutrition supports children’s physical growth, cognitive development and overall learning outcomes. He added that improved infrastructure has contributed to increased enrolment in many public ECDE centres as more parents choose county-supported institutions. Governor Fernandes Barasa on his part maintains that the county remains committed to expanding access to quality early childhood education through sustained investment in ECDE infrastructure across all sub-counties. However, education officers note that although significant progress has been made, some ECDE centres still require additional classrooms, more teachers, learning materials and expanded playgrounds to accommodate the growing number of learners. Parents, on the other hand, have appealed to the county government to sustain the momentum by completing ongoing projects and extending similar investments to all ECDE centres in the region. English: Murkomen urges diaspora to invest in community health services. Kenyans living in the diaspora have been encouraged to complement government efforts in improving access to quality, affordable, and accessible healthcare services through investments in community health facilities. Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen made the appeal on Friday when he presided over the official opening of Kenyaluk Medical Centre in Salawa Division, Baringo Central Constituency. Murkomen said the diaspora community, alongside professionals in the country, plays a significant role in strengthening the health sector by supporting the establishment of modern medical facilities that serve local communities. The CS, who was accompanied by Housing Principal Secretary Charles Hinga, recognized the efforts of the family of Wilfred Kandie, a son of Kipsoit village based in the United States, for constructing the Level 3A medical facility. Murkomen said the hospital is a major investment that will benefit residents of Salawa, Baringo County, and neighbouring Elgeyo Marakwet County. “I have looked at the facility; it is a proper use of money. You can see the space and the modern equipment, and we need more of such facilities,” he said. The CS pledged to support the medical centre in acquiring additional facilities, including a theatre and inpatient services, to enable it to be upgraded to a Level 4 hospital and qualify for funding under the Social Health Authority (SHA). He encouraged more professionals to invest in similar projects, noting that even small initiatives can grow into important community assets in the future. Baringo Central Member of Parliament Joshua Kandie commended Kenyaluk Foundation for giving back to the community through the investment in healthcare. Kandie said the facility demonstrates the positive impact of diaspora contributions in transforming lives and accelerating development at the grassroots level. The founder of the medical centre said the project was inspired by a personal tragedy involving his late father, Mzee Kanyeluk Komen, who died eight years ago from an avoidable lifestyle disease. Kandie said the experience exposed the challenges faced by many residents, particularly men, who often delay seeking medical attention until their conditions become severe. “Most of our community members are seeking medical attention when it is too late, and that is the reality we cannot ignore,” Kandie said. He explained that the project was initiated in partnership with the Kenya Pipeline Foundation and other stakeholders to promote preventive healthcare and encourage early access to medical services. The facility will provide routine medical check-ups for residents while strengthening maternal and child health services within the area. Kandie said the medical centre would reduce the financial burden faced by patients suffering from lifestyle diseases who previously travelled long distances to seek treatment in Kabarnet, Iten, and Eldoret City. He added that plans are underway to expand medical outreach programmes to reach more residents within the surrounding communities. Murkomen said such investments are critical in supporting government efforts to improve healthcare delivery, especially in rural areas where access to specialized services remains a challenge. He urged more Kenyans, both locally and abroad, to consider investing in projects that directly improve the lives of communities. By Benson Kelio

English: Business leaders, investors to gather for SME conference in Nairobi. Business leaders, policymakers, investors and industry experts are set to converge in Nairobi this week for the 3rd Annual SME Conference, Awards & Exhibition organised by the Kenya Private Sector Alliance (KEPSA). The two-day event scheduled for July 23–24, 2026, at the All Saints’ Cathedral Auditorium will be presided over by Chief Guest FCPA Dr. Wycliffe Ambetsa Oparanya, Cabinet Secretary for Cooperatives and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Development. Held under the theme, “Beyond Survival: Building Smart and Resilient Businesses,” the conference is expected to bring together more than 2,500 delegates, including SME owners, policymakers, investors, development partners, financial institutions and industry specialists. The forum will focus on addressing key challenges affecting Kenya’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), including access to finance, market opportunities, innovation, digital transformation and the creation of a supportive policy environment. MSMEs remain a critical pillar of Kenya’s economy, with an estimated 7.4 million enterprises employing about 15 million people and contributing approximately 40 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Despite their contribution, many enterprises continue to face challenges such as limited access to affordable financing, changing market conditions, regulatory barriers and low levels of formalisation. According to KEPSA, the conference will provide practical solutions through discussions on access to finance and investment readiness, market access, trade opportunities, MSME capacity building, innovation, technology adoption and strategic partnerships. Participants will also benefit from keynote addresses, expert panel discussions and an exhibition featuring products, services and innovations from more than 250 exhibitors. The event will also host the MSME Innovation Challenge and MSME Enablers Awards, which will recognise 20 outstanding enterprises for their achievements and contribution to the sector. Other activities include business clinics offering entrepreneurs one-on-one advisory support and networking opportunities connecting SMEs with investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners.
