Busia launches second Mpox vaccination phase as cases rises. The Busia County Department of Health will roll out the second phase of its Mpox vaccination campaign from July 17 to 26, targeting high-risk populations in an effort to curb the continued spread of the disease. The campaign will mainly focus on Matayos and Teso North sub-counties, which have recorded the highest number of infections due to their proximity to the Kenya-Uganda border and increased cross-border movement. Speaking after a stakeholders’ sensitization forum attended by representatives from religious groups, administrators, customs officers, sex workers, fish traders, boda boda operators and the transport sector, Matayos Sub-county Health Promotion Officer Kennedy Odhiambo said the vaccination exercise is aimed at reducing transmission and protecting vulnerable populations. “We are commencing the Mpox vaccination campaign, which will run from Friday, July 17 to July 26. The county has continued reporting Mpox cases, especially in Matayos and Teso North because of the border points and cross-border movements,” said Odhiambo. He noted that Busia has so far recorded 105 confirmed Mpox cases, an indication that community transmission is still ongoing. “There are cases that are being reported and so far in the county we have 105 cases. This clearly indicates that there is still transmission of Mpox which needs to be controlled,” he added urging residents to continue observing preventive measures alongside the vaccination campaign. “Our aim is to ensure the community is free from Mpox. We have been conducting sensitization to ensure people receive the right information and understand the measures they should practice to prevent infection,” he added. An officer from the Infectious Diseases Section, Joan Anyanga, said the campaign will prioritize Matayos and Teso North because they account for the highest number of reported cases. “The vaccination campaign will mainly be conducted in Teso North and Matayos sub-counties because they have experienced the highest number of infections. Matayos has reported 47 cases while Teso North has reported 29 cases, making them the most affected areas,” she said. Anyanga added that disease surveillance and screening remain active across the county to identify new infections early. “We have improved our surveillance and screening to identify cases and respond promptly. The vaccination targets people at risk, and we encourage the community to observe preventive measures, including regular handwashing and following all Ministry of Health guidelines to reduce community transmission,” she advised. Busia Municipality Assistant County Commissioner Calvin Monare on his part called on residents to cooperate with health workers and ignore misinformation surrounding the vaccine. “Vaccination is going to protect us. The disease is still with us, and my appeal is that we cooperate and ensure we get vaccinated. The vaccine is safe and has been approved by the relevant government agency. Let us not be distracted by misinformation and fail to protect ourselves,” he said. A beneficiary of the first phase of the vaccination campaign, George Luhoma, encouraged those eligible to receive the vaccine to do so saying he experienced no adverse effects. “Last year I received the Mpox vaccine and it was good for me. My appeal to those working at the border points is to prioritize getting vaccinated so that they remain safe. There are many myths surrounding this vaccine, but as someone who has received it, I can confirm it is safe,” he said. By Salome Alwanda /Rodgers Omondi

English: Stakeholders review proposed PPP reforms to boost infrastructure development. The government has intensified public consultations on proposed amendments to the Public Private Partnerships (PPP) legal framework as it seeks to improve infrastructure development, attract private investment and address challenges experienced in implementing PPP projects. Stakeholders in Uasin Gishu County were taken through the PPP (Amendment) Bill 2026, the draft PPP (Project Management) Regulations 2026 and the draft PPP (General) Regulations 2026 during a public participation forum held in Eldoret. The consultation, led by the National Treasury’s Public Private Partnerships Directorate, provided citizens, business leaders, government representatives and other stakeholders with an opportunity to review the proposed legal changes and submit their views before the documents are finalized and forwarded to Parliament. Speaking during the forum, PPP Director General Eng. Kefa Seda said public participation was critical in ensuring that the proposed reforms reflect the views and concerns of Kenyans. He said PPPs have become an important mechanism for financing infrastructure projects as the government continues to face fiscal constraints caused by increasing demand for public services and limited resources. “Public Private Partnerships have therefore become vital in bridging the government’s infrastructure funding gap. They provide a viable off-balance sheet solution for continued infrastructure development,” said Seda. He explained that PPPs involve collaboration between the public and private sectors to deliver public functions or services, with private partners receiving compensation through agreed arrangements. Seda noted that although Kenya has made progress in using PPPs to develop infrastructure, implementation challenges and regulatory gaps experienced over the past decade necessitated a review of the existing framework. The PPP Act of 2013, which was amended in 2021 to improve efficiency and provide clearer timelines for investors, has faced practical challenges requiring further improvements. “The country has an aspiration to develop and one of the key catalysts is infrastructure development. Given the fiscal constraints we are facing, Public Private Partnerships provide an alternative mechanism for delivering critical infrastructure projects,” he said. The proposed amendments target three key areas: the PPP Act, the General Regulations and the Project Management Regulations. According to Seda, the changes are intended to improve project delivery, remove uncertainties and provide investors with greater confidence. He said the government is particularly focused on creating a predictable environment that encourages private sector participation while ensuring public interest is protected. The public participation exercise began on July 13 and has already covered regions including Nyanza, Western Kenya and the Coast before moving to the Rift Valley. Similar forums are being conducted in Kajiado and Kitui, with the final consultation expected in Nairobi. Seda encouraged Kenyans, including persons living with disabilities, private sector players and representatives from public institutions, to participate by attending forums or submitting written memoranda through the PPP Directorate’s official platforms. He said all submissions received will be reviewed and considered before the proposed amendments are finalized. The PPP Director General also addressed concerns over delayed government payments to contractors, acknowledging that fiscal challenges had contributed to pending bills affecting some projects. He, however, said the government had introduced measures to clear outstanding payments, enabling contractors to resume work. “We are happy to report that many contractors have resumed work after the government securitized funds to facilitate payment of pending bills,” he said. Seda added that ensuring investor confidence requires guarantees that contractual obligations will be honoured on time. He said the government was working with international financial institutions, including the African Trade and Development Bank (TDB) and the World Bank, to establish credit enhancement mechanisms such as partial risk guarantees aimed at reducing payment risks for investors. He explained that after completion of the public participation process, the Directorate will analyze the submissions, incorporate suitable proposals and undertake a validation exercise before presenting the revised drafts to stakeholders. The proposed amendments will then be submitted to Parliament, which will conduct its own public participation process before debating and considering the legislation. Uasin Gishu Deputy County Commissioner Mathew Yego Baroni urged stakeholders to actively participate in the process, saying their views would help shape government policy and planning. Baroni said public participation is a constitutional requirement under Articles 10 and 118 of the Constitution of Kenya, which promote democratic governance and citizen involvement in decision-making. He encouraged stakeholders to use the opportunity to provide constructive feedback that would strengthen the PPP framework and ensure it serves the needs of Kenyans. The forum was attended by representatives from the PPP Directorate, including Faith Pesa from the Legal Department, Project Officer Elijah Kirimi and other technical officers. By Ekuwam Sylvester

Government livestock restocking revives Igembe North families after banditry. Residents of Igembe North are rebuilding their livelihoods following the government’s livestock restocking programme aimed at compensating families that lost cattle to bandit attacks and restoring economic stability in the region. The exercise, being coordinated by the National Government in collaboration with local leaders and security agencies, has seen hundreds of cattle distributed to verified beneficiaries to help revive livestock farming, improve household incomes and strengthen food security. Speaking at Mea Primary School during the second day of the exercise, Igembe North Officer Commanding Police Division (OCPD) Jerald Okari Marando said the distribution had progressed peacefully despite isolated attempts by a few individuals to obtain livestock fraudulently. Marando said 175 cows were distributed on the first day, bringing the total number of cattle issued under the programme to 207. The initiative targets families whose livestock was stolen by bandits between 2023 and 2026. He said the government expects to distribute about 600 cattle under the programme and urged residents who have not yet benefited to remain patient as more animals are expected. The OCPD warned that adequate security personnel had been deployed to safeguard the exercise and ensure that only verified beneficiaries receive the livestock. “We will not allow anyone to interfere with this process. Security officers are on the ground to ensure transparency and fairness so that genuine victims benefit from the programme,” he said. Igembe North National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) Manager Ronald Mugambi commended the government for intervening to restore the livelihoods of families that had suffered devastating losses due to years of cattle rustling and banditry. Mugambi urged beneficiaries to retain the animals for breeding and dairy production instead of selling them, noting that the programme is intended to rebuild herds, increase milk production, improve household incomes and enhance long-term food security. Beneficiaries welcomed the initiative, saying it had restored hope after years of hardship. Stephen Kamendo from Amwathi Ward thanked the government for the livestock donation and appealed to residents yet to receive cattle to remain patient, expressing confidence that additional livestock would be distributed. Joshua Muriki, a resident of Mea, recalled the anguish of watching bandits drive away their livestock, saying many families had been left without their primary source of income and food. He said the restocking programme had given affected households an opportunity to rebuild their lives and regain economic independence. Former Igembe North Member of Parliament and Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS) Board Chairman Joseph M’Eruaki welcomed the initiative but called for fairness, transparency and accountability throughout the distribution process. Speaking earlier during a church service at Athiru Catholic Church, M’Eruaki said only registered victims of cattle rustling should benefit from the programme and cautioned against favouritism or political interference. He also urged beneficiaries not to sell the livestock, saying the government’s objective is to rebuild herds, support dairy farming and restore sustainable livelihoods across the region. By Kamanja Maeria

Government to spend Sh10 million to desilt Kosowe Earth dam. The National Government through National Drought Management Autbority (NDMA) will spend Sh10 million to desilt Kosowe Earth Dam in Nzaui Subcounty with a view to increase its water capacity to 30,000 cubic meters, Makueni County Drought Co-ordinator (CDC) Alice Munyao has disclosed. Munyao made the disclosure in a County Steering Group meeting held at the County Commissioner’s Boardroom on Friday where she said that the desilting of the dam will take only three months to complete by October when the short rains are anticipated. The County Coordinator also revealed that the dam will benefit over 3,000 households with a view to end their perennial shortage of water in the area. “The works to desilt the Kisowe Earth Dam started on 16th July, and expect to be completed by early October before the short rain season commences,” Munyao said in the meeting that was chaired by the Deputy County Commissioner (DCC) who is also Personal Assistant in the County Commissioner’s office Peter Kimani on Friday. However, she never gave the name of the contractor undertaking the works at the dam. Also, she revealed her organization will spend another Sh3 million to purchase 300 Gala Goat that is aimed at improving the breed under the project and benefit 32 Nzakika Community groups. While saying goats are being procured currently, Munyao said that through the project, seeks to improve low goat productivity and household resilience in the Arid and Semi -Arid (ASAL) area hence help address poor genetics, inbreeding and climate stress with a view to improve the breed. She further said that the intervention is also expected to enhance growth rates, milk production and market value while maintaining adaptability to the harsh conditions in the area. The project is being implemented through the Wee Community Based Organization (CBO) in collaboration with NDMA and County Livestock Services at the county government. “The expected results include higher household incomes, improved nutrition and food security, better herd performance and strengthen community resilience, with sustainability ensured through revolving breeding schemes, skills transfer and strong institutional and community ownership,” she said. During the meeting the members were taken through the performance of the last rains of March, April and May that came earlier and was fairly distributed but farmers experienced reduced production because the reduction of rains that impacted on the crops. A Technical Committee was constituted comprising of the departments of Water, Health, Education, Agriculture, Livestock and NDMA to go and evaluate the impact of seasonal rains and other shocks on food and nutrition security and bring a report to be deliberated by the County Steering group on 24/07/2026. By Patrick Nyakundi

English: Ematete farmers’ field day promotes climate-smart agriculture innovation. Farmers, agricultural stakeholders, government officials, development partners and agribusiness companies converged at the Ematete Agribusiness Centre in Vihiga County for the fifth Ematete Agribusiness Farmers Field Day to promote climate-smart agriculture, innovation and sustainable agribusiness development. The event, held on Friday under the theme “Enhancing Climate-Smart Agriculture and Agribusiness Innovation,” attracted hundreds of farmers from across the county who interacted with agricultural experts, viewed modern farming technologies and learned practical approaches to improving productivity while adapting to the effects of climate change. The field day was presided over by Vihiga County Chief Officer for Agriculture Betty Mulianga, who urged farmers to embrace climate-smart agricultural practices to safeguard food production amid increasingly unpredictable weather patterns. She said agriculture remains the backbone of Vihiga County’s economy and encouraged farmers to adopt improved seed varieties, efficient water management technologies and modern production methods to increase yields and household incomes. “Climate change is no longer a future challenge but a present reality. We must adopt innovative farming methods that protect the environment while increasing productivity and improving farmers’ incomes,” Mulianga said. She assured farmers that the county government remains committed to strengthening agricultural extension services, supporting agribusiness development and working with development partners to improve food security and economic growth. Mulianga noted that extension officers continue to equip farmers with knowledge on sustainable farming practices, soil conservation, crop diversification and climate adaptation to help them cope with changing weather conditions. Mwibona Ward Member of the County Assembly Zakayo Manyasa urged residents to embrace commercial agriculture by viewing farming as a business rather than a subsistence activity. He said equipping farmers with modern knowledge, technologies and entrepreneurial skills would create employment opportunities, improve household incomes and strengthen food security within the county. Manyasa challenged young people to venture into agribusiness, saying agriculture offers numerous opportunities for wealth creation through crop production, livestock farming, value addition and agricultural marketing. The event featured exhibitions by farmers, agribusiness companies and agricultural organisations showcasing improved crop varieties, livestock products, certified seeds, farm machinery, irrigation technologies, value-added agricultural products and climate-smart farming innovations. Farmers also demonstrated practical farming techniques, giving participants an opportunity to observe and learn best practices that can be replicated to improve productivity and resilience on their own farms. The Cereals Growers Association (CGA), led by Benson Omukhago, highlighted its efforts to strengthen cereal production through farmer training, access to quality farm inputs, collective marketing and promotion of climate-smart agricultural practices. Omukhago encouraged farmers to adopt improved cereal production technologies, diversify their farming enterprises and strengthen producer organisations to enhance bargaining power and improve market access. He said empowering farmers with technical knowledge and reliable markets is essential for building resilient and profitable agricultural value chains capable of withstanding climate-related challenges. Seed Co representatives, led by Benjamin Kidigi, exhibited a range of certified and improved seed varieties developed to help farmers increase productivity and adapt to changing climatic conditions. Kidigi educated farmers on the importance of using certified seeds, observing proper crop management practices and selecting crop varieties suited to different ecological zones to maximise yields. He urged farmers to embrace improved seed technologies as an effective way of increasing food production, enhancing household food security and improving farm profitability. The field day also strengthened partnerships between farmers, government agencies, private companies, financial institutions and agricultural organisations through discussions on market access, sustainable agriculture, climate resilience and agribusiness innovation. Participants expressed appreciation for the opportunity to interact directly with experts and exhibitors, saying the event equipped them with practical knowledge, new technologies and market information that would help improve farm productivity and increase household incomes. The event concluded with renewed calls for sustained collaboration among government, development partners, research institutions, private sector players and farming communities to accelerate agricultural transformation, strengthen climate resilience and promote sustainable food production in Vihiga County. By Henry Ananda and Kelly Barasa

Government promotes horticulture farming to boost farmers’ incomes. Farmers in Southern Nyanza have been encouraged to embrace horticulture farming as a profitable venture capable of improving household incomes and creating sustainable livelihoods. Former Horticulture Development Authority (HCDA) official and horticulture expert John Rono said crops such as passion fruits, vegetables and tomatoes provide farmers with reliable earnings because they generate income on a daily or weekly basis. Speaking during a passion fruit farming exhibition at Ayego Passion Fruits Groups Farm, Rono said horticultural produce has ready markets locally and internationally throughout the year, unlike some traditional crops whose returns are affected by market fluctuations. He noted that many farmers in the region have continued to rely heavily on maize and sugarcane despite facing persistent challenges associated with the two crops. Rono expressed concern that horticulture production in the region remains low because nearly 99 per cent of farmers concentrate on large-scale maize and sugarcane farming. “Horticulture fruits have a wider market which spreads from Nairobi to Kampala in neighbouring Uganda. Farmers should take advantage of this opportunity by putting more land under fruit and vegetable production,” he told farmers attending the two-day exhibition sponsored by AMPATH. He said the exhibition provided farmers with an opportunity to learn modern horticulture farming technologies, including irrigation, greenhouse farming and shade-net production. Rono urged farmers to diversify their agricultural activities by adopting high-value crops that can provide consistent income and reduce dependence on traditional crops. He added that increased production of fruits and vegetables in Southern Nyanza would help reduce reliance on supplies from other regions and create opportunities for local farmers. Tomatoes, passion fruits and other horticultural products continue to have strong demand in markets across the country, but production in the region remains insufficient. Farmers were encouraged to take advantage of available technologies and market opportunities to transform horticulture into a major source of income and economic growth. By George Agimba

Governor Mutai orders crackdown on unlicensed milk vendors. Kericho Governor Dr. Erick Mutai has ordered an immediate crackdown on unlicensed raw milk vendors and brokers, declaring that the purchase, aggregation and distribution of raw milk outside the county’s licensing framework is illegal. The governor said the county government would intensify enforcement against illegal milk aggregators to protect dairy farmers from exploitation and ensure milk is marketed through licensed channels. He noted that strengthening cooperative societies remains central to the county’s strategy to improve farmers’ earnings by eliminating middlemen who deny producers fair returns. Dr. Mutai said the county would continue investing in the dairy sector through milk cooling plants, feed mixers, artificial insemination services and Enterprise Development Programme (EDP) grants to registered cooperative societies. He said the interventions are intended to increase milk production, improve quality, promote value addition and enable farmers to earn higher incomes. “Our focus is to build strong cooperative societies that can collect, process and market farmers’ milk competitively. We will continue investing in cooling infrastructure, animal feeds, quality breeding and farmer empowerment because a stronger dairy sector translates into better household incomes, more jobs for our youth and sustained economic growth for Kericho,” said Dr. Mutai. The governor made the remarks during the funeral service of the late schoolteacher and farmer Ann Chebochok at the Kericho Golf Club Grounds on Friday. Besides addressing dairy sector reforms, Dr. Mutai called for urgent measures to curb the rising number of road fatalities, saying improved highways must be accompanied by enhanced road safety interventions. He urged the national government to fast-track the installation of speed cameras, improve hazardous sections of roads, strengthen enforcement of traffic laws and intensify public awareness campaigns aimed at reducing accidents and protecting road users. “Every life lost on our roads is a reminder that we must do more. We need a combination of better road designs, strict enforcement of traffic regulations and the use of technology such as speed monitoring systems to prevent reckless driving and save lives,” he said. Chebochok, the sister of former Bomet Governor and current Judicial Service Commission Vice Chairperson Isaac Ruto, died in a road accident along Nairobi’s Southern Bypass. According to her family, the accident occurred a few minutes before 6:00 a.m. A post-mortem examination established that she succumbed to severe internal organ injuries sustained in the crash. Her daughter, who was travelling with her, survived the accident after sustaining minor injuries and was discharged after receiving medical attention. Dr. Mutai described Chebochok as a dedicated teacher, accomplished farmer and community leader whose commitment to agriculture and public service positively impacted many lives. He said continued support for farmers and stronger agricultural cooperatives would help preserve the legacy of hardworking producers like her while promoting sustainable economic development in the county. The funeral service brought together national and county leaders, including Principal Secretary for the State Department for Water and Sanitation Julius Korir, Bomet Governor Prof. Hillary Barchok, Kericho Woman Representative Beatrice Kemei, Isaac Ruto, family members, friends and hundreds of mourners who gathered to celebrate Chebochok’s life, honour her contribution to society and stand with her family during the difficult period. By Kelox Mutai

English: Diversification pays off as North Rift maize farmers count losses. As prolonged dry spells continue to slash maize production across the North Rift, a Uasin Gishu farmer who shifted to high-value, climate-resilient crops is earning nearly Sh1 million annually, offering a practical example of how diversification can cushion farmers against climate change and unstable markets. David Kwambai, 71, of Kapsoen Village in Moiben Sub-county, abandoned reliance on maize and invested in coffee, avocado and macadamia farming, transforming his four-acre farm into a profitable agribusiness while many maize growers grapple with declining yields. His success comes as agricultural experts and regional leaders urge farmers to reduce dependence on maize by embracing crops that are more resilient to changing weather patterns and command better market prices. Kwambai told the Kenya News Agency (KNA) that he began growing coffee in 2015 with about 100 trees before gradually expanding to about 2,000 trees after realizing the crop generated better returns than maize. “I started coffee farming in 2015 with about 100 trees, and over time I increased the number to around 2,000. Although prices were not very good in the beginning, I realized coffee was still more profitable than maize,” he said. He said his coffee harvest initially averaged between 300 and 400 kilograms but is expected to exceed 1,000 kilograms this season due to improved farm management and favourable prices. Kwambai sold last year’s coffee through a cooperative society at about Sh700 per kilogram, describing cooperative marketing as a key factor in improving farmers’ incomes. “Coffee harvesting takes about two to three months, but with good care, the returns are worth it,” he said, although he identified coffee berry disease as his biggest production challenge. Seeking to spread risk, the farmer later ventured into avocado and macadamia farming after losses in cabbage and passion fruit production caused by disease outbreaks and poor markets. His 500 avocado trees, planted on two acres, produce between 50 and 80 kilograms of fruit per tree, with the produce selling at an average of Sh110 per kilogram. “Avocado farming is doing very well because of export demand. We harvest about three times a year, giving us a steady source of income,” he said. Kwambai has also embraced sustainable farming practices by producing compost from fallen avocado leaves, cow dung and urea to improve soil fertility and reduce production costs. However, he cited pests, diseases, cold weather and inadequate irrigation water as the major constraints affecting avocado production. His macadamia enterprise is also showing promising returns. Having planted the crop in 2018, he harvested about 300 kilograms of nuts last year and sold them at Sh150 per kilogram. “This year I expect even better yields. Macadamia is a long-term investment, but it pays off,” he said. Beyond crop production, Kwambai practices apiculture and livestock farming to diversify his income further. He keeps 10 beehives, six of which are active, producing up to 200 kilograms of honey every three to four months depending on weather conditions. He also rears dairy cows and goats, which provide additional income while supplying manure used to enrich soil fertility on the farm. Although he has access to water from a drilled source, Kwambai said he has not fully adopted irrigation, noting that expanding irrigation would significantly improve productivity during prolonged dry spells. He identified marketing as another challenge facing farmers, saying coffee growers benefit from cooperative marketing structures while avocado farmers largely depend on brokers because of inadequate storage and cooling facilities. “We need proper storage and cooling plants to reduce post-harvest losses, especially for avocados, which are highly perishable,” he said, adding that farmers are considering forming cooperatives to strengthen their bargaining power. Kwambai appealed to the county and national governments to subsidize farm inputs and deploy more agricultural extension officers to train farmers on modern production methods, soil testing and climate-smart agriculture. He also encouraged young people to embrace agriculture as a business, saying farming can generate sustainable livelihoods when managed professionally. “Even at my age, I am still actively farming and employing young people. Agriculture has great potential if farmers embrace the right crops,” he said. His experience reflects growing calls for North Rift farmers to diversify into drought-tolerant, high-value enterprises as erratic rainfall and prolonged dry spells continue to undermine conventional maize production. Thousands of maize farmers across the region are experiencing reduced yields because of changing weather patterns, highlighting the risks of relying on a single crop and reinforcing the importance of climate-smart agriculture, improved market access and enterprise diversification in building resilient farming systems. By Fredrick Maritim

English: Religious leaders condemn political violence. Religious leaders under the Spiritual Churches Council of Kenya have strongly condemned the recent incident of political violence reported in Keumbu, Kisii County on July 3, 2026, where goons allegedly attacked the Linda Mwananchi convoy. Speaking in Migori Town, the clergy, led by Dick Okuku, urged politicians to exercise tolerance and conduct peaceful campaigns while cautioning young people against being manipulated into engaging in violence for political interests. “We are urging our Gen Zs and other youths to desist from being used and manipulated by the political class to settle their political scores”, said Okuku. The church leaders, however, commended Migori County political leadership for embracing peaceful coexistence, noting that the county has witnessed a significant reduction in political violence compared to the past. They reaffirmed their commitment to working with political leaders, the public, and other stakeholders to promote peace, unity, and issue-based politics as the country prepares for the upcoming General Election. “We are now 13 months to the next general elections, and we urge both the county and national leaders to exercise utmost political restraint, show respect, maintain peace and unity to have a prosperous country,” said Okuku. Mary Robi, also a clergy member, explained that as clergies, they will continue praying for the nation to achieve a peaceful election for the betterment of society. She urged the youth to remain focused and achieve what they want through the ballot instead of being allowed to be used cheaply by the political class. Robi noted that it is so painful to lose a child through political violence, adding that every life is sacred. She commended the Migori political class for showing great restraint and political tolerance in recent weeks and urged them to continue promoting peace and unity for the advancement of the socio-political and economic agendas. by Makokha Khaoya

English: Man sentenced to life imprisonment for defiling toddler. By S, KNA A father of eight who pleaded not guilty to defiling his 17- months- old niece at his house has been jailed for life by a Kericho court. Kericho Senior Resident Magistrate Japhet Bii found Justus Kipsigei Cheruiyot, 46, guilty of defiling the toddler in his house on 1 May 2025 at Chesingoro village in Bureti sub-county within Kericho County. Cheruiyot was also charged with an alternative charge of committing an indecent act with the young child to which he also pleaded not guilty. The prosecution produced six witnesses, all who gave corroborating evidence against the accused. The court heard that on 1, May 2025, the toddler’s mother at around 10.20am, was woken up from her nap by her four- year- old daughter with information that her 17- months- old sibling was being killed by the accused whom he had taken to his house while armed with a knife. The child’s mother on rushing out of her house, met the accused who is her brother fleeing as he dropped her crying toddler to the ground. The mother found her naked child having lost consciousness with blood oozing from her genitals and mouth. She took her toddler to Kapkatet sub-county hospital for treatment where they were brought to Kericho Referral Hospital in an ambulance and the child was taken for surgery and admitted at the facility for 12 days. The matter was reported to Litein police station and the accused was arrested at around 5pm on May 1, 2025. A clinical officer who examined the minor told the court that indeed the toddler had been defiled. A P3 form and laboratory reports tabled before the court indicated that the hymen had been freshly torn and there was bleeding of her private parts. Sexual activity had taken place with penetration as observed with the broken hymen further confirming the defilement charge. A birth certificate was tabled before the court revealing the toddler was indeed 17- months- old at the time of the heinous ordeal. In his defence, the accused gave a sworn testimony and denied committing the offence. He told the court that he did not know what had happened that day. Cheruiyot added that he was arrested and taken to the police station where he was informed that he had defiled a child. He further told the court that the child was usually in the company of her mother and there was no way he would have defiled his niece. In mitigation, the accused pleaded for leniency asking for a non-custodial sentence as he had eight children who depended on him but the magistrate found him guilty and ordered that he serves life imprisonment. “I have considered the mitigation. I have also considered the circumstances which the offense was committed. The accused person committed a beastly act upon a child of tender age that was savage. It is more disturbing that the child belongs to the accused sister who lives in the same compound. From the foregoing, I find that the elements required to prove a case as this have been properly established. There was penetration of a minor by the accused person. The case against him has properly been proved. The accused is hereby found guilty as charged. He is consequently convicted under section 215 of the Criminal Procedure Code (Cap 75) laws of Kenya.” Bii ruled. The convict was reminded of the right to appeal the sentence within 14 days if dissatisfied.

St. Mary’s Mission Hospital, Kakamega paid Sh98 dues. By G, KNA Cabinet Secretary for Health Aden Duale has announced release of Sh98 million owed to the troubled St. Mary’s Mission Hospital in Mumias, Kakamega county paving way for its reopening. Speaking to the press outside the Kakamega County Governor offices after a meeting, Duale also announced that the government will in the next two weeks’ pay Kakamega County Sh100 million being part of the claims from SHA and that further reimbursements will be done once the ongoing verification of all claims is concluded. “By 14th of this week, the date SHA pays reimbursements, we shall pay Kakamega county Sh100 million and the remaining balances to be paid out once verification of all claims are concluded,” he added. Duale said the Ministry has put in place an AI Powered detection system that monitors every transaction real time, detecting suspicious patterns and blocking fraudulent claims. On St. Mary Mission hospital is Mumias run by the Kakamega Catholic Dioceses, ceased operations last month due to financial issues and alleged non-remittance of funds by the Ministry of Health. However, Duale said the hospital has since December last year to August this year, been reimbursed a total of Sh98 million. The CS said the hospital will receive another reimbursement of Sh14.3 million in the next two weeks, but said they have agreed with Bishop Joseph Obanyi of Kakamega Diocese on how the remaining balances will be cleared, once verification is concluded. “So from where we sit St, Mary’s hospital has not been closed by SHA, nor by the regulator Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentist council, or the Digital Health Agency that controls the system and their license valid to operate. The CS said on reopening of the health facility, he will preside over a donation of a consignment of drugs from the government and a medical camp at the facility for area residents,” he added. “Those who are peddling rumors in funerals and to use St. Mary’s hospital for political mileage to look for something else to talk about”, he said, in an apparent reference to some politicians who have been calling for his resignation over non-remittance of claims to health facilities countrywide. Duale said the Ministry of Health will in the next two weeks unveil a Digital Tracking System in all public health facilities to curb theft of medical commodities. “We have put in place a water tight solid system to ensure that no staff can steal any medical commodities, not even a Panadol and the system will be operational in all public health institutions in two weeks’ time.” he added. Kakamega Diocese Bishop Joseph Obanyi, who also addressed the media said that they had had fruitful discussion with the CS and his team and confirmed that St. Mary’s Mission hospital had received a total Sh98,671,567 Million from SHA since December last year to August this year. “We have pending claims of Sh35 million that we expect to receive from SHA which will help us clear the arrears for workers’ pay,” he said. “We also have pending Sh10 million still being verified by SHA and will continue engaging,” said Bishop Obanyi. The Bishop said strike of workers at the health facility that led for ceasing of medical services was due to accruing salary arrears of 3 months from defunct National Health Insurance FUND (NHIF), which stands at Sh143 million. Bishop Obanyi added that once they receive another pending claim of about Sh14 million, when the necessary documentation and verification is concluded in the next two weeks, then St. Mary’s Mission Hospital will engage the workers to resume work. Kakamega Governor Fernandez Barasa said Kakamega County has registered a total of 800,000 people under SHA against its target of 1.8 Million people “We have embarked on a serious registration exercise to register the remaining one million people and I urge the residents to turn up and register in order to benefit”, he added. Barasa said Kakamega County is still owed Sh293 Million pending bills from SHA, Sh72 Million being for level two and threes, 55 Million for level fours and Sh166 million for level Kakamega County Teaching and Referral Hospital, which is level 5. The governor confirmed that SHA will pay the county Sh100 million, being part of the reimbursement of the pending bills for Kakamega County and Teaching Referral hospital in the next two weeks. “We are still awaiting an analysis of 15 level four public health facilities and level two hospitals,” he added. Present were the Principal Secretary Medical Services Dr. Ouma Oluga and the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of SHA Dr. Mercy Mwangangi among others.

Turkana intensifies preparations for Community Conservancy Board elections. The Turkana County Government, in partnership with the Northern Rangelands Trust (NRT), has intensified public engagement activities in Letea, Turkana West Sub-County, to prepare residents for the election of members to the Community Conservancy Board. The initiative seeks to strengthen community participation in natural resource management while laying the foundation for effective governance of the proposed conservancy. The ongoing programme includes stakeholder consultations, community capacity building and the development of a Community Conservancy Action Plan aimed at equipping residents with the knowledge required to participate meaningfully in the election process. The exercise is being led by County Director of Natural Resources Pauline Ng’oli and NRT Team Lead Moses Kinapu in collaboration with local administrators, community leaders and other stakeholders. Speaking during the public engagement forum, Ng’oli said the process is intended to ensure the Community Conservancy Board is established in accordance with the law and begins operating on a strong institutional foundation. “We have chosen to work closely with administrative structures, local institutions, community leaders and residents to establish a board that will effectively manage the proposed conservancy,” she said. Ng’oli noted that involving local communities from the outset would enhance transparency, accountability and community ownership of conservation programmes. Residents welcomed the initiative, saying the training had increased their understanding of the community conservancy model and prepared them to elect capable leaders. “We now have a better understanding of the community conservancy model and how it operates. As a community, we feel ready for the elections,” said Letea resident Mariao Peyonon. NRT Team Lead Moses Kinapu emphasised the importance of conducting free, fair and transparent elections, noting that residents could choose board members through either a secret ballot or consensus, depending on what the community agreed. Kinapu cited successful examples from conservancies such as Nasalot, where community conservancy boards have strengthened natural resource management, promoted environmental conservation and improved livelihoods. The County Government and NRT said they are promoting the community conservancy model in Letea and other parts of Turkana West to enhance environmental conservation, encourage community participation in natural resource governance and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for local residents. By Peter Gitonga

Coastal residents urged to back government development agenda. Cabinet Secretaries Salim Mvurya (Youth Affairs, Creative Economy and Sports) and Hassan Joho (Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs) are actively urging residents in the coastal region to support the national development agenda. The two leaders emphasized the importance of community collaboration with the national government in driving sustainable economic activity, job creation, and the equitable use of public resources. Mvurya and Joho, accompanied by a host of local leaders, were speaking at Ronald Ngala grounds in Mombasa County during a meet-the-people engagement. They were accompanied by Mombasa Governor Abdulswamad Shariff Nassir, Senator Mohamed Faki; MPs Mohamed Machele (Mvita), Badi Twalib (Jomvu), Rashid Bedzimba (Kisauni), Mishi Mboko (Likoni) and Principal Secretary for Youth Affairs, Fikirini Jacobs. Ministers Mvurya and Joho, who are past two-term governors of Kwale and Mombasa, respectively, said policy continuity was critical to sustaining economic reforms, improving security and delivering long-term prosperity. The two defended the Kenya Kwanza administration’s record on regional equity, saying development was now being shared fairly across the country. “We want the people to continue supporting the bottom-up economic growth strategy of the national government,” said Mvurya. CS Mvurya reaffirmed the National Government’s commitment to creating opportunities for the youth to enable them to participate meaningfully in the country’s socio-economic development. Mvurya cited the Sh5 billion National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) project, which he noted is a bold intervention that will foster socio-economic stability in the long run. He said the NYOTA project, championed by the national government, is potentially a ‘panacea to the widespread youth unemployment’ and associated social ills in the country. Mvurya said the government will continue upskilling young people and creating an enabling environment where they can thrive. He said they will continue to crisscross the coastal counties of Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi, Lamu, Taita Taveta and Tana River with elected leaders to promote peace and unity ahead of the 2027 general elections. Mvurya said they will continue engaging coastal residents to back the government development agenda on account of its commitment to advancing national development through sustained investment in priority sectors aimed at strengthening service delivery. On his part, CS Joho expressed the government’s commitment to accelerating meaningful development and expanding opportunities for the youth. He said the meet-the-people forums are focused on strengthening infrastructure, expanding economic opportunities, empowering the youth and enhancing service delivery while underscoring the importance of sustained public participation in shaping the development agenda. “We urge coastal residents to continue supporting the national government in its endeavor to undertake transformative development programmes in every corner of the country,” said Joho. Joho urged residents not to gamble with their future in the forthcoming 2027 general polls, warning that a wrong electoral decision could set back an entire generation. He said major infrastructure and economic projects in the coastal region include the Dongo Kundu Bypass (Mombasa), Mwache Multipurpose Dam (Kwale), LAPSSET Corridor (Lamu), and the proposed Mombasa-Nairobi expressway. “All these mega projects are geared toward transforming regional trade, water security, and transportation,” he said. Joho said the government will continue implementing programmes that promote inclusive development and enhance the quality of life for the citizenry. Governor Nassir urged the youth to avoid challenges such as drug and substance abuse, which he decried as a worrying reality affecting the society. The coastal county boss urged the youth to shun drug abuse and criminal activities to protect their personal health and secure a prosperous future. By Hussein Abdullahi

Maalim urges Northern Kenya residents to register as voters. Mandera Deputy Governor Dr. Ali Maalim has called on residents of Northern Kenya to register as voters, saying higher voter registration will strengthen the region’s political influence ahead of the 2027 General Election. Speaking during an Annual General Meeting (AGM) of a school in Mandera, Dr. Maalim urged all eligible residents to take advantage of the ongoing Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR) exercise being conducted by the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC). He appealed to residents of Mandera, Wajir, Garissa, Marsabit, Isiolo, Tana River and Turkana counties to register in large numbers, saying the pastoralist region must fully demonstrate its electoral strength. “We want everybody to take advantage of the voter registration exercise. I urge all the people of Mandera and Northern Kenya to ensure they register as voters. As pastoralist communities, we must demonstrate our numbers and ensure our voices are heard,” said Dr. Maalim. The Deputy Governor said increased voter registration would enhance the region’s voice in national decision-making and ensure its interests are well represented in future political processes. Dr. Maalim also reaffirmed his political support for President William Ruto, saying the region remained firmly behind the Head of State ahead of the 2027 polls. “Our direction is very clear. We are supporting President William Ruto, and we are not wavering on that position,” he said. His remarks come as the IEBC continues with Voter Registration exercise across the country to enlist new voters before the next General Election. According to IEBC statistics, 97,859 new voters have been registered across the North Eastern region during the exercise. Garissa leads with 24,575 new voters, followed by Marsabit (23,267), Wajir (21,171), Mandera (18,214) and Isiolo (10,632). Nationally, the commission has registered 2,345,476 new voters during the 30-day mass voter registration campaign, bringing the total number of newly registered voters since continuous registration resumed in September 2025 to 2,612,725. The IEBC, together with political leaders and civic organisations, continues to encourage eligible Kenyans, especially youth and first-time voters, to register and participate in the country’s democratic process. By Adan Mohamed

English: Tharaka Nithi plans constituency museums to preserve culture for future generations. The Tharaka Nithi County Government will establish small museums in each constituency to preserve and promote the county’s cultural heritage, Governor Muthomi Njuki has announced. Speaking during the closing ceremony of a two-day Chuka Igambang’ombe Cultural Festival at Kaanwa Chiefs’ Camp, Njuki said the museums will showcase cultural artifacts, traditions and the history of communities across the county while serving as learning centres for residents, students and visitors. The governor directed the County Department of Culture to allocate funds for the initiative in the next county budget, saying the project is intended to safeguard the county’s rich heritage for future generations. “We must not allow our culture to disappear because it defines who we are. Our children should know their traditions and heritage,” Njuki said, expressing concern that many young people have limited knowledge of their cultural roots. He called on parents, elders and community leaders to take a leading role in passing cultural values, customs and traditions from one generation to another. Njuki said the county government would continue supporting community-based organisations, artists and cultural groups to strengthen efforts aimed at preserving and promoting local traditions. He noted that cultural festivals provide important platforms for celebrating identity, promoting unity and educating younger generations about their heritage. The governor also announced that the county’s flagship Ura Gate Cultural Festival will be held in August, with the exact date to be communicated later. He said the event will bring together communities from across Tharaka Nithi to celebrate the county’s cultural diversity through performances, exhibitions and traditional activities. Commending the success of the Chuka Igambang’ombe Cultural Festival, Njuki said the large turnout and colourful performances reflected residents’ commitment to preserving their cultural heritage. He praised the 25 cultural dance groups, artists, organisers and residents who participated in the festival for keeping traditional practices alive and encouraging cultural appreciation among young people. The governor also appealed to residents to protect wildlife by avoiding the killing of wild animals, saying conservation is essential in preserving Kenya’s natural heritage for future generations. On leadership, Njuki cautioned residents against embracing politics based on regional or clan interests, saying no constituency can elect leaders without support from others. Instead, he urged voters to evaluate leaders based on their development record, integrity and commitment to serving all residents equally, regardless of their place of origin. Maara Member of Parliament Kareke Mbiuki said annual cultural festivals play a vital role in preserving traditions while strengthening community identity, unity and social cohesion. Mbiuki commended the county government for supporting cultural groups and organising constituency cultural festivals, saying the initiative would help safeguard Tharaka Nithi’s rich cultural heritage for generations to come. By Christine Ngitori and Glory Kiende

Tharaka Nithi rolls out projects to boost trade. The Tharaka Nithi County Government has unveiled a multisectoral development programme for Kaanwa Trading Centre in Mariani Ward, featuring road infrastructure, a modern market,improved healthcare and coffee revitalization to spur economic growth and improve livelihoods. Governor Muthomi Njuki announced the projects while launching the Kaanwa market roads paving project, saying the investments are part of the county’s broader strategy to modernise trading centres and improve access to essential services. He said the county government will pave roads within Kaanwa market to enhance accessibility and mobility, noting that the trading centre falls under Kathwana Municipality and will benefit from the municipality’s development initiatives. “Good town infrastructure, especially roads and markets, is a key driver of economic growth and would restore the dignity of our traders,” the Governor said. Njuki further announced that the county government will construct staircases for all shops in the market to improve accessibility, safety, and the general outlook of the trading centre. The Governor also revealed that rehabilitation of the MitheruKaanwa road is underway to enhance connectivity, ease transportation and facilitate movement of goods and services. In the health sector, Njuki said the Kaanwa Maternity Facility will soon be opened, bringing maternal healthcare services closer to residents. On agriculture, the Governor urged farmers in Mariani Ward to embrace coffee farming, saying research had confirmed that the crop can perform well in the area. He said the county government will allocate funds in its budget for the construction of a coffee factory in Mariani Ward to support value addition and improve farmers’ earnings as part of broader efforts to strengthen coffee production and revive the sub-sector. “We want Mariani to be the leading coffeeproducing ward in Tharaka Nithi County. Research has shown that coffee can thrive here, and we will continue investing in the sector to unlock its full potential,” Njuki said. By Dickson Mwiti and Christine Ngitori

English: Goverment launches hassle-free mobile ID cards enrollment exercise. By H, KNA The State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services has launched a hassle-free mobile enrollment exercise for the issuance of national identity (ID) cards dubbed Usajili Mashinani. The Usajili Mashinani is a people-centred initiative designed to reduce barriers to registration and ensure citizens fully benefit from the ongoing national government projects and social services across the country. Local opinion leaders have been urged to support the new initiative by encouraging all eligible people to show up for enrolment. State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services Principal Secretary (PS) Dr. Belio Kipsang says the new registration drive seeks to make the vital document accessible to all Kenyans, especially those residing in difficult-to-access areas. Dr. Kipsang urged eligible citizens to take advantage of this new ID campaign which will be characterized by mobile registration efforts. The PS urged administrators to support and expedite legitimate applications, provide accurate registration data, and support public awareness, noting that access to identification is a constitutional right and critical to socio-economic inclusion. “All registration officers are expected to uphold the highest standards of professionalism and discipline as corruption will attract punitive measures,” he said. The PS encouraged citizens to acquire national IDs to access government services, highlighting that over 400,000 users access the eCitizen platform daily, all of whom require a valid ID. Dr. Kipsang said to enhance mobile registration, the government has deployed 100 live capture machines, with additional units set to be rolled out nationwide to further intensify registration across the country. The initiative uses mobile units to target remote areas and pastoralist communities with a goal to reducing the time it takes to receive ID cards to a week. “This live capture technology will allow on-the-spot registration of citizens in remote areas with data transmitted real-time for processing within the shortest time possible,” said Dr. Kipsang. The PS commended chiefs and assistant chiefs for their continued efforts in the registration of persons. He said the government will use the ID cards scheme as a ‘reliable comprehensive data base’ to plan for the present and future generations. “The government is working overdrive to ensure that no Kenyan who turns 18 years and above is denied access to their rightful identity,” he said. He says the current identity cards issuance effort, specifically targets Kenyans residing in far-flung areas, where national registration offices do not exist. The PS was speaking in Hola town, Tana River county, accompanied by heads of directorates from the State Department, where he led a sensitization programme, engaging National Government Administrative Officers (NGAOs) on the Revised National ID registration guidelines. The sensitization focused on familiarizing administrators with the revised framework and emphasized the importance of expanding mobile registration outreach to ensure all eligible Kenyans access identification services. Dr. Kipsang called on National Government Administrative Officers(NGAOs) to strengthen grassroots sensitization, ahead of the upcoming 10-day intensive mobile registration exercise across Tana River county, reinforcing Usajili Mashinani as a key driver of inclusive service delivery. The PS said to accelerate the process, the government has eliminated mandatory intensive vetting for border counties placing such responsibility on local chiefs and their assistants to verify new applicants. He said the mandatory vetting in border counties was abolished by President Dr. William Ruto in May 2024, as it has placed many hurdles and created unnecessary bureaucracy denying many vital documents. Dr. Kipsang said similar sensitization engagements have been successfully conducted in Kilifi, Kwale, Taita Taveta, and Mombasa counties, strengthening grassroots coordination and delivery of registration services. He encouraged citizens to take advantage of this opportunity to obtain their ID cards, which are essential for participating in national activities including the upcoming 2027 general elections. “Usajili Mashinani is an initiative that will ensure that every eligible citizen is registered, empowering Kenyans to participate in the country’s growth and development,” he said. He said his office is determined to work towards ensuring that every Kenyan is accounted for and has access to their rightful identity and take part in nation building. The PS said that the government remains dedicated to preserving the integrity of Kenyan citizenship for ‘national pride and security’. “National government officials should ensure that the ID card issuance process to capture the populace proceeds smoothly in their areas of jurisdiction,” said the PS, adding that ID cards has a pervasive impact on every facet of the socio-economic fabric of the nation. ID cards serve as a critical document required for obtaining a taxpayer identification number, opening a bank account and applying for jobs, voters card and passport. They are also required for accessing social protection services including the Inua Jamii Cash Transfer programme for vulnerable populations such as the elderly.

Tinderet farmers face poor maize harvest due to drought. Farmers in Tinderet Sub County are facing the prospect of one of the poorest maize harvests in recent years after erratic rainfall disrupted crop development, raising concerns over food shortages, rising maize prices and declining household incomes. Agricultural experts estimate that maize production in the sub-county could decline by between 30 and 40 per cent compared to a normal season, following prolonged dry spells experienced during critical stages of crop growth, particularly flowering and grain filling. Tinderet Sub County normally produces between 90,000 and 100,000 bags of maize annually, but this season’s output is projected to drop to between 55,000 and 65,000 bags due to moisture stress affecting thousands of hectares under maize production. Agronomist Peter Kiprono said inconsistent rainfall patterns had significantly reduced the yield potential of maize farms across the area. “The rainfall distribution was highly unreliable. While some locations received heavy downpours, they were followed by prolonged dry spells that stressed the maize crop at the most critical growth stages. We expect yields to decline sharply across most parts of the sub-county,” he said. According to the Ministry of Agriculture, maize is grown on nearly 18,000 hectares in Tinderet Sub County every year and contributes more than 60 per cent of household food requirements. However, field assessments have shown that many farms have been affected by moisture stress, with farmers reporting stunted crops, poorly filled cobs and reduced yields. In Songhor-Soba, Chemilil-Chemase and Kapchorua wards, farmers who expected to harvest between 20 and 25 bags of maize per acre now anticipate collecting only eight to 15 bags per acre. Farmer John Keter from Meteitei said the poor harvest would negatively affect his family’s food security and income. “We invested heavily in certified seeds and fertiliser, but the rains failed us. Instead of harvesting about 120 bags from my six-acre farm, I expect barely 60 bags. That means I will have to buy maize before the end of the year,” he said. Agricultural economist Jane Chebet warned that climate variability had become a major threat to food production in the region, urging farmers to embrace climate-smart farming practices. “The traditional rainfall seasons are becoming increasingly unpredictable. Farmers should adopt drought-tolerant maize varieties, water harvesting technologies and conservation agriculture to minimise production losses. Diversifying into crops such as beans, sorghum and millet will also improve resilience,” she said. The expected decline in production is likely to affect maize prices, with consumers facing higher costs due to reduced supply. A 90-kilogramme bag currently retailing between Sh4,800 and Sh5,200 could rise to between Sh6,000 and Sh6,500 later in the year if production shortages persist. Economists said reduced harvests would also affect household incomes because many farmers depend on maize sales to meet essential needs such as school fees, medical expenses and other family obligations. With fewer bags available for sale, households are expected to experience reduced disposable incomes, affecting spending power and local economic activities. Livestock farmers are also likely to feel the impact of the poor maize harvest as reduced availability of maize stalks could create shortages of animal feed during the dry season. This may force farmers to purchase supplementary feeds at higher costs. Food security advocate Grace Jepkemboi called for urgent measures to support vulnerable households and strengthen resilience among farmers. “Families that depend almost entirely on maize for food will be the hardest hit. We need greater investment in irrigation, climate-smart farming, timely weather information and crop diversification to safeguard food security,” she said. Stakeholders said increased investment in irrigation, access to reliable weather forecasts, improved extension services and promotion of drought-resistant crops would help farmers cope with changing weather patterns. Nationally, maize accounts for more than 65 per cent of Kenya’s staple food consumption, with the average Kenyan consuming about 98 kilogrammes annually. A significant decline in production from major maize-growing regions such as Tinderet could therefore contribute to supply shortages and increased prices across the country. By Sammy Mwibanda

English: Garissa Public Service Board fully constituted after members sworn in. The Garissa County Public Service Board has been fully reconstituted following the swearing-in of three new members, paving the way for the board to resume full operations and strengthen public service management in the county. The ceremony, held at the Garissa County headquarters, was presided over by Garissa Chief Magistrate Thomas Mwangi, who administered the oath of office to Abdikadir Gure Farah, Naima Hassan Farah and Muhumed Abdi Oyow. The appointments restore the board to full membership after vacancies arose following the expiry of the terms of three former members. Garissa Governor Nathif Jama, accompanied by Deputy Governor Abdi Dagane, congratulated the new members and urged them to begin their duties immediately, noting that residents expect a fully functional board capable of improving service delivery. The Governor called on the board, led by Chairman Ahmed Abdirahman, to strengthen public service management, promote professionalism and ensure the county maintains an efficient and stable workforce. He further challenged the board to support measures aimed at containing the county wage bill while ensuring recruitment is based on merit and transparency. Jama said a professional public service is essential for maintaining continuity in government operations, even during periods of political transition. The Governor also urged the board to undertake payroll cleansing to eliminate irregularities and ensure that only qualified personnel are employed in the county public service. He said the exercise would enhance accountability, improve efficiency and promote quality service delivery to residents. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by County Commissioner John Cheruiyot, County Secretary Mohamud Mursal, Members of the County Assembly led by Sankuri MCA Abdirahman Mohamed, Township Sub-County Administrator Shaiya Hambe, as well as family members and friends of the newly appointed board members. By Mohamed Dahir

Government expresses optimism over economic growth. National Treasury Principal Secretary Dr. Chris Kiptoo has assured Kenyans that the country’s economy remains stable, saying the government has made significant progress in restoring macroeconomic stability despite global economic shocks experienced over the past few years. Speaking in Gichugu, Kirinyaga County, Dr. Kiptoo said the economy had faced major external challenges from 2022, including the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war, which triggered high inflation, depreciation of the Kenya shilling and increased pressure on public debt management. “The external factors manifested in a very big way. Domestic prices went up, inflation rose to almost 9.6 per cent, the shilling came under a lot of pressure and we experienced challenges in managing our debt,” Dr. Kiptoo said. He noted that through deliberate government interventions over the last three years, the economy has steadily recovered. “In the last three years or so, we have worked very hard to stabilize the economy. Inflation has come as low as almost 2.7percent, but still went back to around 4.4 percent. We have stabilized the shilling, as you are aware,” the PS added. Kiptoo also encouraged Kenyans to invest in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, noting that investors who entered the stock market in recent years have more than doubled their investments due to improved market performance. “Macroeconomic stability has been achieved, and the stock market has performed exceptionally well. Those who invested have seen significant returns,” he said. Despite the gains, Dr. Kiptoo acknowledged that the government continues to face fiscal challenges, particularly in balancing revenue collection with rising public expenditure. “Everybody wants money, yet revenues are not growing as fast as our spending needs. This forces us to finance budget deficits. However, we remain committed to fiscal consolidation because it is in the country’s best interest to reduce debt and sustain economic stability,” he said. On the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, Dr. Kiptoo said Kenya has so far been shielded from severe economic impacts due to the resilience built over the past three years. “We have put in place measures to ensure the country continues to have adequate energy supplies despite the prevailing global uncertainties,” he added. PS Kiptoo also used the platform to appeal to Kenyans to remain united, saying national cohesion is essential for development. “We have a great country, and we have no other country but Kenya. Every time we face challenges, we overcome them because we are resilient. Let us continue promoting unity, love one another and work together for the good of our nation,” he said. His sentiments were echoed by Principal Secretary for the State Department for Forestry, Gitonga Mugambi, who urged Kenyans to uphold peace and patriotism. “We have a duty to love our country and take care of one another. Whatever our differences, we are one people and we are all Kenyans. We must ensure Kenya remains a country that we all cherish,” Mugambi said. The leaders were attending the burial of Josphat Simon Karinga Njagi the father of Dr. Jane Wangu Njuguna, Chief Executive Officer of the Kenya Forestry Research Institute (KEFRI). By Mutai Kipng’etich

Title deeds restore hope to former Kihiumwiri land dispute victims. Residents of the former Kihiumwiri Land Buying Company settlement in Murang’a County are beginning a new chapter after decades of violent land disputes, following the Government’s land regularisation programme that has seen hundreds of title deeds issued to legitimate landowners. The exercise gathered momentum after Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome recently issued 750 title deeds to beneficiaries and directed a 90-day verification exercise to authenticate land ownership records before additional titles are processed. The settlement, now commonly known as Kenyatta Farm, was for years associated with violent land conflicts, prolonged court battles and disputed ownership claims that claimed lives, displaced hundreds of families and left many residents living in fear. Officials of Kihiumwiri Land Buying Company said the verification exercise is progressing well and is expected to be completed by the end of August, paving the way for the issuance of thousands of remaining title deeds. Company Director Josephat Thiongo said the exercise involves reconstructing historical land records to eliminate irregularities that had previously been exploited by land cartels. “We are rebuilding the registries to prevent any attempts to interfere with official records. This process will ensure that only genuine shareholders receive title deeds,” said Thiongo. He said completion of the verification exercise would enable the processing of the remaining title deeds and bring lasting certainty over land ownership in the settlement. According to company officials, the conflict claimed the lives of seven directors, while five others disappeared under mysterious circumstances and have never been traced. The violence also forced hundreds of families to flee their homes as disputes over land ownership intensified. Residents say the ongoing issuance of title deeds has restored confidence, reduced tensions and encouraged peaceful coexistence among people who were once divided by the conflict. Naomi Wanjiku, one of the beneficiaries whose husband was killed during the land clashes, described receiving a title deed as the end of years of uncertainty. “I am happy because I now know I will not be evicted from the land where I have lived for many years,” she said. She explained that residents are receiving title deeds for the parcels they currently occupy, while those whose original allocations correspond to undeveloped land retain ownership of those plots. The community is also seeking formal recognition of the name Kenyatta Farm in place of Kihiumwiri, saying the new identity symbolises reconciliation, peace and a fresh beginning after decades of violence, disappearances and prolonged legal battles over land ownership. By Muoki Charles

Youth urged to utilize ICT hubs for digital opportunities. Youth in Turkana have been urged to make use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) hubs in Lodwar to enhance their skills and tap into opportunities in the digital economy. Deputy County Secretary Joseph Nyanga made the appeal during a tour of ICT hubs in Lodwar, where he was accompanied by officials from the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF). Nyanga said the County Government will work closely with UNICEF through the Directorate of Vocational Training to address challenges affecting the smooth operation of the ICT hubs. He encouraged ICT hub operators to benchmark with successful service providers locally and internationally to improve the quality of services offered. The visit brought together officials from UNICEF and the county government, including Directorate of Vocational Training Director Stephen Eregae, his deputy Jeremiah Loyapan, and representatives from ICT, ECDE, partnerships, and vocational training centres. By Peter Gitonga

Kwale plants 2800 fruit tree seedlings to mark Mazingira day. By H, KNA Some 2800 fruit tree seedlings have been planted in Kwale county to mark this year’s Mazingira Day. The fruit tree planting exercise at Mavirivirini Primary School in Mwavumbo Ward, Samburu Sub-County of Kwale was led by Deputy Governor Chirema Kombo and County Commissioner (CC) Stephen Orinde. The countrywide tree planting campaign took place under the theme, “Citizen-Centric Tree Growing and Environmental Stewardship.” This year the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Forestry has urged all Kenyans to trace their primary school roots in a bid to donate and help in planting fruit trees on Mazingira Day marked annually on October10. The national government has set a target of 100 million fruit trees planted annually, translating into a budget of Sh1 trillion in 3 years. Deputy governor said the devolved government remains committed to protecting the environment and ensuring sustainable water for all. Kombo has urged area residents not only use the Mazingira Day to do tree planting, but also make it a habit of planting trees round the year. He highlighted the essential role trees play in absorbing carbon dioxide and protecting water catchment areas. “Since the national government directive of planting 15 billion trees by 2030 Kwale County has planted over 600,000 seedlings,” said Kombo. Speaking during the event, Chirema urged area residents particularly those from arid and semi-arid areas of Samburu, Kinango and LungaLunga sub counties to take the tree planting initiative seriously to curb the adverse climatic changes affecting the area. The DG noted the importance of tree planting in the arid and semi-arid zones adding that the initiative will help restore degraded land while improving livelihoods of local communities. “We have to change the narrative of our land and not just planting trees but growing fruit trees that will help us grow economically,” he said. On his part, Orinde said the national government works hand in hand with the county governments to make sure climate and environmental aspects are taken care of for the benefit of Kenyans. “The national government has many projects and we implement them together with the county government so that we change the harsh conditions for our people particularly in areas of Samburu Kinango and LungaLunga Sub-Counties,” he said. The CC urged residents to be intentional in planting and caring for tree seedlings, stressing that trees help in fighting climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. He said Kenya is facing an environmental crisis as a result of global warming, requiring collective action from all and sundry to combat the adverse effects of climate change. The CC explained that the choice of fruit trees by the government was deliberate, noting that besides their environmental benefits, they also provide a sustainable source of income for the people. “Let each one of us plant and nurture at least a tree not just for ourselves, but for our environment and posterity,” said Orinde.
